data.title: Strongly consider updating `hdf5-pure` to latest
data.body:
Hi, new owner of [hdf5-pure](https://github.com/CramBL/hdf5-pure) here

I'm a long time contributor to [hdf5-rust](https://github.com/metno/hdf5-rust) and author of 70% of the issues on `hdf5-pure`.

I noticed that you are running an old version (in terms of churn/bug fixes) and there are MANY bug fixes since, that fixed cases where the reader either panicked or silently misinterpreted data.

https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/blob/f057ae9a5efd90314a7b9042380db947a147c1bb/Cargo.toml#L294

The reader also handles `libver` bounds better and supports many more data types.

Most of the open bugs are related to writing HDF5 files, and I'm working on it.

The previous owner Stephen Berry, was forced to either archive the project or transfer ownership due to a policy at his job. My employer is thankfully very supportive of open-source, so I could take over.

The project has now moved from a heavy agent driven project, to a much more rigorous human-driven (still AI assisted) approach, which is what I believe is needed to reach a quality where I can use it in software deployed on millions of embedded devices (which I plan to do).

`rerun` is obviously very serious high-stakes software too, so part of my agenda with this issue is to help ensure the quality of `rerun` (through encouraging you to update) and another part is to hopefully instill confidence in the future development of `hdf5-pure`.

data.title: Fix decoder resets on consecutive live keyframes
data.body:
### Related

No linked issue. Reproduced with live JPEG `EncodedImage` playback in 0.37.1.

### What

Live image playback can keep showing an old frame and a loading indicator even when decoding finishes between player updates.
At the live edge, each new JPEG starts a GOP after the last enqueued sample, which `enqueue_samples` treats as a skip: it resets the decoder before consuming its completed output.

Preserve the decoder when the requested sample is exactly the next sample to enqueue, allowing the existing loop to continue into the new GOP.
Actual forward skips and backward seeks retain their reset behavior.

Add deterministic regression tests for consecutive image keyframes, growing multi-frame GOPs, forward skips, and backward seeks.
The two continuous-playback tests fail on the original code; all four pass with the fix.

data.title: Speed up seconds-only duration formatting
data.body:
### Why

Continuing my pass through the repo for small, isolated performance wins.

Seconds-only duration formatting is used when displaying timestamps and durations, including per-frame UI paths.

### What

Write seconds-only durations directly into one preallocated string instead of constructing and joining separately allocated fragments.

| Case | Before | After | Reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Milliseconds | 474.34 ns | 57.02 ns | 88.0% |
| Microseconds | 624.75 ns | 83.66 ns | 86.6% |
| Nanoseconds | 827.86 ns | 116.92 ns | 85.9% |
| Large duration | 992.22 ns | 130.49 ns | 86.8% |

A temporary allocation benchmark also measured a reduction from 17 allocations/reallocations to 1 for nanosecond-precision formatting.

The existing formatting behavior is preserved, with additional coverage for explicit signs and `i64::MIN`.

### Testing

- `cargo test --all-features --no-fail-fast -p re_format`
- `cargo test --all-features --no-fail-fast -p re_log_types`
- `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets -p re_format`

`cargo nextest` was unavailable in my local environment, so I used `cargo test`.

### Agent

🤖 AI disclosure: I used Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol at xhigh reasoning effort to help identify the allocation, implement the optimization, and construct the local benchmarks. I have reviewed and understand the resulting implementation.

data.title: Cache point cloud GPU uploads across frames
data.body: ### Related * Part of #1136 ### What The viewer currently re-uploads every point cloud's data (positions/radii, colors, picking ids) to the GPU on every frame, even when nothing changed — the main remaining action item from #1136. This PR caches the uploaded data textures and reuses them across frames. **`re_renderer`:** the upload is split out of `PointCloudDrawData::new` into a new persistent `GpuPointCloud` (the three finished data textures + point count). `PointCloudDrawData::from_gpu_cloud(..)` then builds only the genuinely per-frame state: the "all points" bind groups (they embed the per-draw-data radius-boost uniform), per-batch uniform buffers/bind groups, and transparent-sort data. The existing immediate-mode `PointCloudBuilder::into_draw_data()` path is reimplemented on top of the same split, so there is a single upload code path and other callers are untouched. `PointCloudBatchInfo` gains an optional `first_point_index` so multiple batches can address overlapping ranges of one upload, and `sort_positions` becomes `Option>>` (also removing a per-frame `Vec` clone in the transparent-sort path). **`re_view_spatial`:** `Points3DCpu` — already memoized on `query_result_hash` — now also holds an `Arc`, uploaded once on cache miss. Per frame the visualizer only builds `PointCloudBatchInfo`s (transform, flags, highlights, picking id) referencing the cached upload. Invalidation and eviction ride on the existing generation-based `Points3DCache`; the cache implements `vram_usage()` so the memory panel accounts for the textures. As a side effect this also fixes the `TODO(grtlr)` where N instance transforms re-uploaded the same cloud N times — they are now N batches over one upload. Behavior is intended to be unchanged (shading, alpha blending + back-to-front sorting, outlines incl. per-instance highlight ranges, picking, labels, bounds). The relevant snapshot tests (`point_shading`, `transparent_geometry`, `keypoint_rendering`, `select_box_instances`, `transform_clamping`, `transform_hierarchy`, `draw_order`, `gaussian_splats3d`) pass; `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `cargo test` on `re_renderer`/`re_view_spatial` are clean. Natural follow-ups (left on the immediate-mode path for now): `points2d` and `gaussian_splats3d`, which have the same per-frame re-upload structure. ### Benchmarks Headless harness reusing the repo's own snapshot-test infra (`TestContext` + `egui_kittest`): one static opaque `Points3D` entity with N seeded random points; per frame, `step()` = visualizer execution + draw-data creation + upload staging, `render()` = submit + offscreen readback ending in `device.poll(Wait)` so GPU time is included. 10 warmup + 100 measured frames, baseline/branch interleaved A/B/A/B, 2 repetitions. Ryzen 9 9950X3D, RTX 5070 (driver 580.173.02, Vulkan), rustc 1.96.0, `--release`. Baseline `b5dbd31` (v0.36.2) vs this branch. Median ms/frame on the RTX 5070 (rep1 / rep2): | N points | phase | baseline | this PR | speedup | |---:|---|---|---|---| | 1 M | full frame | 4.14 / 4.15 | 2.11 / 2.19 | **1.9×** | | 1 M | step (CPU + upload) | 2.43 / 2.48 | 0.72 / 0.73 | 3.4× | | 5 M | full frame | 15.12 / 15.17 | 5.11 / 5.11 | **3.0×** | | 5 M | step | 9.65 / 9.72 | 0.81 / 0.84 | 11.8× | | 10 M | full frame | 28.43 / 28.35 | 8.91 / 9.00 | **3.2×** | | 10 M | step | 18.47 / 18.45 | 0.89 / 0.90 | 20.6× | p90 tracks the medians (10 M: 29.4 → 9.6 ms); rep-to-rep spread is ≤1.1%. The signature is exactly what the change predicts: per-frame CPU/upload cost becomes independent of N (0.72 → 0.89 ms from 1 M to 10 M) instead of linear (2.4 → 18.5 ms). On llvmpipe the CPU-phase win is the same (10 M: 18.5 → 1.1 ms) but total frame time is rasterization-dominated and too noisy to claim. Caveats, honestly: this is the best case for the cache (static scene, one opaque entity, one transform); a scene whose data changes every frame pays the same upload as before (during warmup, deliberately not charged to either side). Headless readback serializes CPU/GPU, so the full-frame ratio is an upper bound — the step-phase result is the robust one. Happy to share the harness (single self-contained test file) if useful. ### Agent 🤖 This PR was opened by a coding agent (Claude Code, model Claude Fable 5), directed by @kaashmonee. Confidence: the mechanism follows the maintainers' own roadmap item from #1136 ("cache uploads, so we only upload when the points change"), reuses the existing `query_result_hash`-keyed memoization for invalidation, and is validated by the existing snapshot tests plus the benchmarks above. Kept in draft pending human review of the code; design feedback welcome in the meantime.

data.title: Allow configuring the segment count of 2D primitives such as Ellipses2D
data.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Currently, `Ellipses2D` appears to always use 32 segments per ellipse. At high zoom levels, this can become visibly noticeable as the ellipse looks slightly polygonal rather than smooth.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

I would like to be able to configure the number of segments used to render primitives such as `Ellipses2D`.

For example, it would be useful to increase the segment count for higher visual quality, or decrease it when rendering performance is more important.

Ideally, this could be exposed as a property such as:

`ellipse.with_segment_count(128);`

The exact API is of course open for discussion.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Currently, I work around this by logging a circle/ellipse as a `Mesh3D` and generating the geometry myself with the desired number of segments.

This works, but is considerably less convenient than being able to configure the segment count directly on the corresponding primitive.

**Additional context**

The main use case is viewing ellipses at high zoom levels, where 32 segments are sometimes not sufficient to make the shape appear smooth.

Having a configurable segment count would also allow users to trade off visual quality against rendering performance depending on their use case. It would be great if a similar option could eventually be available for other primitives that approximate curved shapes using a fixed number of segments.

data.title: Interest in upstreaming re_renderer changes from a downstream fork (browser WGSL fixes, atomics-wasm, WebGL2 picking, optional crates)?
data.body:
Hello — asking before writing PRs, so I don't send you work you don't want.

We build a node-based 3D modeller ([Akatela](https://github.com/virtualritz/akatela)) on `re_renderer`, and have carried a fork for a while (~23 commits on top of `main`, plus merges). Some of it is clearly ours and belongs nowhere near upstream; some looks like it fixes things you'd hit too. I'd rather ask which, if any, you want than open a pile of PRs.

**Probably useful to you -- portability and build-shape fixes, no behaviour change:**

1. **Browser WGSL strictness** (3 small shader fixes): add `return` after `discard` in the mesh picking layer; replace a trailing `if/else`-return pattern; use `var` + trailing return in `camera_ray_to_world_pos`. Some browsers' WGSL front-ends reject the current forms.
2. **Multi-threaded (atomics) wasm support** -- plus making `re_web::fs` optional so atomics-wasm builds at all, and silencing dead-code warnings the atomics config produces in the error tracker.
3. **WebGL2-compatible mesh selection** via the Limited device tier, for machines where WebGPU is unavailable or falls back to a software adapter.
4. **`re_video`/`re_byte_size`/`re_tuid` behind feature flags**, for consumers that only want the renderer.
5. **Relaxing the `wasm-bindgen` `=0.2.108` pin** to `0.2`.
6. **Slope-scaled depth bias** for overlay lines and points.

**Ours, and I'd expect you to say no -- listing for completeness:** matcap shading (including an `use_matcap == 0` albedo-at-corner-UV path), external depth-texture sharing with premultiplied compositing and depth-only/picking-only mesh modes, per-face `element_id` picking with a selection SSBO and hover/selection tinting, a wireframe selection cue, and a glam 0.33 bump (you're on 0.30, so that one is a fork artefact, not a proposal).

**Questions**

- Is any of group 1–6 worth a PR? I'd send them separately and small, each rebased on current `main`.
- For the WGSL fixes specifically: would you want them as-is, or do you have a preferred idiom for shaders that must pass every browser front-end?
- If the answer is "none of it", that's a genuinely fine answer and saves us both time -- I'll keep them downstream and stop wondering.

Happy to provide the diffs or a branch for anything you want to look at first.

data.title: Improve TextLog view performance
data.body: ### Related * Closes https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/7562 ### What Speed up the TextLog view by only querying the view range of text logs instead of EVERYTHING! #### How Previously the visualizer did a range query for **EVERYTHING** and materialized every textlog entry on each frame, just to figure out how many rows it had and where to scroll to. This scales linearly with the amount of `TextLog`s logged! 😱 This is fine for a few text logs, but the viewer grinds down to 5fps for recordings with 500k lines (https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/7562). The fix is to stop querying the actual data to create the view layout and instead create the layout using chunk metadata. Chunks already know their time range and `TextLog` counts, so that's enough to derive the total row count and which rows fall where in time. This lets us only query the data for the currently visible time range. Additionally this replaces the view's current `egui_extras::TableBuilder` rendering with `egui_table` which supports virtual scrolling over a known number of rows (we already do this for the dataframe view!). Filtering by log levels through the blueprint is a bit complicated, since it requires log level component information from inside each chunk. But since chunks are immutable (right?), we can get around this by scanning a chunk once and caching the per-level row counts by `ChunkId`. This new approach also doesn't support rendering multi line logs, the data is shown when hovering. Implementing this makes the accounting a lot more tedious and should be done as a followup. --- However, this does mean a `TextLog` row's level/color must come from that row alone, which means blueprint overrides/defaults for them are no longer applied. Also, level/color no longer carry follow the latest-at semantics (which I think is fine for this archetype, and actually desired?)

data.title: Move the .ply file readers out of re_sdk_types and into re_importer

labels.name: 🚜 refactor
labels.description: Change the code, not the functionality

data.body:
`re_sdk_types` currently contains `.ply` parsing for two archetypes:

* `crates/store/re_sdk_types/src/archetypes/points3d_ext.rs`
* `crates/store/re_sdk_types/src/archetypes/gaussian_splats3d_ext.rs`

Both are almost entirely about the file format rather than about the log type. Our log-type definitions shouldn't carry format-specific IO — that belongs in `re_importer` (or a reader crate it owns), which is where every other format lives.

A direct `Archetype::from_ply_*` constructor would only make sense for something like a `GaussianSplats3DPly` with an opaque blob component, which is not what these are.

Raised by @grtlr in https://github.com/rerun-io/reality/pull/2621#discussion_r3620919768; deferred out of that PR to keep the diff reviewable.

data.title: Inversion of Colormaps for DepthImage
data.body: When visualizing DepthImages, small values (close points) are mapped to a dark color and large values (far away points) are mapped to a bright color when using any of the available sequential color maps. For our application, it would be more useful to invert the color map. We usually care more about close points than far away points, so it's more intuitive to have close points highlighted in a bright color. **Describe the solution you'd like** A toggle switch that allows to invert the color map in the view selection would be the optimal solution. This gives more flexibility in how the available (and very useful selection of) colormaps can be applied. **Describe alternatives you've considered** An alternative would be to add general support for custom color maps - this would however be less neat, as we would then just add another Turbo color map, but with an inverted spectrum. **Additional context**

data.title: Allow consumers to remove the `ring` transitive dependency
data.body:
## Title

Allow consumers to remove the `ring` transitive dependency

## Summary

Rerun currently forces a transitive dependency on [`ring`](https://crates.io/crates/ring) onto anyone who depends on the viewer or SDK crates.
It would be good to make `ring` optional / overridable, so that consumers who prefer a different cryptography backend (most commonly [`aws-lc-rs`](https://crates.io/crates/aws-lc-rs)) can avoid pulling `ring` into their build at all.

## Motivation

The rustls project no longer treats `ring` as the recommended default cryptography provider — as of rustls 0.23 the default is `aws-lc-rs`, and `ring` is only used when explicitly opted into via the `ring` crate feature.

> While Rustls itself is platform independent, by default it uses [`aws-lc-rs`](https://crates.io/crates/aws-lc-rs) for implementing the cryptography in TLS.

— rustls crate docs, <https://docs.rs/rustls/latest/rustls/> (the `ring` provider is described as available only "with the `ring` crate feature enabled").

Consumers embedding Rerun in a larger application often already standardize on `aws-lc-rs` (or a specific FIPS-validated / audited crypto backend) and want a single crypto provider across their dependency tree.
Today Rerun makes that impossible: `ring` is unconditionally dragged in, so these consumers end up with two crypto backends compiled in, or cannot satisfy their own supply-chain / crypto-policy requirements.

## Where `ring` enters Rerun's dependency graph

There are two independent entry points:

1. **`re_auth` (`oauth` feature)** uses `ring::signature` directly for RS256 JWT verification.
   - `crates/utils/re_auth/Cargo.toml`: `ring = { workspace = true, optional = true }`, gated behind the `oauth` feature.
   - `crates/utils/re_auth/src/crypto_provider.rs`: `use ring::signature as ring_sig;` (RSA PKCS#1 SHA-256 verification).
   - This is the dominant path: `re_auth` → `re_perf_telemetry` → `re_datafusion` → … → `re_viewer` → `rerun`, so essentially the whole viewer graph inherits `ring`.

2. **`rerun_py`** selects `ring` as the rustls crypto provider.
   - `rerun_py/Cargo.toml`: `rustls = { workspace = true, features = ["ring"] }`.

(For reference, the workspace already pins `rustls = { version = "0.23.40", default-features = false }` and `ring = "0.17.14"` in the root `Cargo.toml`, and `reqwest` is configured with `rustls-tls`.)

## Possible implementations

Listed roughly from "most flexible for consumers" to "simplest":

1. **Force the consumer to choose the crypto provider.**
   Expose no default crypto backend from the crates that need one; require the downstream application to install a rustls `CryptoProvider` and to supply the RSA-verification backend for `re_auth`.
   Most flexible and most explicit, but the biggest breaking change and the most friction for simple consumers / examples.

2. **Depend on `ring` by default, but allow it to be overridden (cfg / Cargo features).**
   Keep the current behavior out of the box, but add mutually-exclusive features (e.g. `crypto-ring` vs `crypto-aws-lc-rs`) on `re_auth` (and a matching knob for the `rerun_py`/rustls selection) so a consumer can turn `ring` off and select `aws-lc-rs` instead.
   For `re_auth`'s RS256 path this means abstracting the RSA verification behind a small trait or feature-gated module rather than calling `ring::signature` directly.
   Non-breaking default, opt-in migration path.

3. **Switch to `aws-lc-rs`.**
   Replace `ring` with `aws-lc-rs` outright (both the rustls provider feature and the `re_auth` RS256 verification).
   Simplest end state and aligns with rustls' current default, but `aws-lc-rs` has a C/build-toolchain (cmake/NASM) footprint that may be undesirable for some targets (notably wasm and some cross-compilation setups), so it may need to remain feature-selectable anyway.

## Notes / open questions

- Any solution needs to cover **both** entry points above, not just the rustls feature — otherwise `re_auth`'s direct `ring::signature` use keeps `ring` in the tree.
- wasm builds and cross-compilation should be considered when picking between `ring` and `aws-lc-rs`, since their C-toolchain requirements differ.
- A feature-based approach (option 2) is likely the least disruptive first step and can coexist with a longer-term move toward option 3.

data.title: Go SDK

labels.name: 🪵 Log & send APIs
labels.description: Affects the user-facing API for all languages

data.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Rerun ships SDKs for Python, Rust, and C++. A lot of robotics *data infrastructure* — ingestion services, job workers, object-storage plumbing — is written in Go, and there is currently no way to produce or read the Rerun format from it.

One practical consequence: when a Go-based pipeline needs to emit a derived artifact for visualization, MCAP is reachable (`github.com/foxglove/mcap/go/mcap`) and RRD is not. So the choice gets made by SDK availability rather than by what suits the viewer — and the RRD-only capabilities (footer manifest, on-demand chunk loading via `rerun server`) stay out of reach for that whole class of services.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Not the full SDK — the write path would cover most of it:

- recording stream: `init`, `set_time`, `log`
- a core set of archetypes (scalars, transforms, points, images)
- `save` to `.rrd`

No viewer, no `spawn`, no gRPC client.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- **Shell out to the `rerun` CLI** — workable, but means shipping the CLI in worker images and treating its behavior as an API.
- **A Python sidecar just to call the SDK** — a second runtime and deployment unit for one function.
- **Emit MCAP instead** — the viewer reads MCAP natively, so this gets you visualization without RRD. It's the pragmatic answer today, at the cost of the RRD-only capabilities above.

**Additional context**

I searched issues and discussions and didn't find an existing request for Go, so this is to gauge interest rather than to assert demand. If it's out of scope, that's a useful answer too — in that case, documenting the supported way to produce RRDs from outside the three SDK languages (a stable CLI contract, or format-stability guarantees for third-party writers) would cover most of the need.

data.title: Harden server-backed chunk streaming
data.body:
### What

This tightens the native server-backed chunk query path and adds the first user-facing Hugging Face registration path for #11315:

1. Direct HTTP Range fetches now fail closed when the remote store does not behave like a range-safe object store.
2. Non-drift direct-fetch failures now fall back to the `FetchChunks` gRPC proxy instead of failing the query outright.
3. The adaptive `PipelineBudget` defaults are lowered from effectively-disabled values to real larger-than-RAM backpressure defaults.
4. The REDAP Python e2e suite now has a scrub/seek regression check, plus `scripts/redap_scrub_metrics.py` for measuring narrow seek queries against an external REDAP server, remote registered prefix, or Hugging Face dataset repo.
5. `DatasetEntry.register_huggingface(...)` resolves `.rrd` files from a Hugging Face dataset repo into canonical `resolve/` URLs and registers them as remote RRD sources. The metrics harness can use this via `--hf-repo`.
6. The local OSS REDAP server can now register `http://` / `https://` RRD URLs as lazy range-backed stores. It reads footer/manifest ranges up front, then emits direct URL chunk metadata so native clients can fetch selected chunks from the original HTTP(S) object store without downloading the full RRD locally or proxying all bytes through REDAP.
7. `FetchChunks` fallback now also understands direct RRD chunk keys, so a failed direct fetch can still be served by the REDAP server from the same HTTP range-backed source.

For direct fetches, the client now:

- sends `Accept-Encoding: identity` alongside the byte `Range` request
- requires `206 Partial Content` instead of accepting any successful 2xx response
- requires `Content-Range` matching the requested byte window
- requires `Content-Length` matching the requested byte count
- stops reading as soon as the response body exceeds the validated range length
- rejects short bodies before decoding
- falls back through `FetchChunks` gRPC for non-source-drift direct failures

`416 Range Not Satisfiable` is also treated as non-retryable. Source-changed direct failures remain terminal so stale manifests do not get hidden by a fallback path.

For query memory backpressure, the default budget moves from the old effectively-unbounded settings:

- fraction: `1.0` -> `0.25`
- min per partition: `4 GiB` -> `64 MiB`
- max per partition: `1 TiB` -> `1 GiB`

### Why

For larger-than-RAM / on-demand dataset access (#11315), accepting a `200 OK` after sending `Range` is dangerous: it means the server may have ignored the range header and returned the entire object. Even if headers look right, a broken server should not be able to make the client allocate more than the byte window it asked for.

At the same time, users should still be able to query through the storage node when direct object-store access is unavailable or misconfigured. The gRPC fallback preserves that path without allowing accidental full-object direct downloads.

Separately, the existing `PipelineBudget` machinery already tracks decoded bytes, gates segment concurrency, releases bytes during safe-horizon GC, and has a stall breaker. But the old default clamps (`4 GiB` min, `1 TiB` max) meant the budget basically never applied in normal use. Lowering these defaults makes the existing remote query pipeline apply real backpressure by default while still allowing env overrides via `RERUN_PIPELINE_BUDGET_*`.

The new scrub e2e test covers the interaction that matters for viewer-style scrubbing: sample `(segment, index)` seek points from index-range metadata, seek those narrow slices, and assert they push down filters, stay on one segment, and fetch/plan less than a full scan. The script version is intentionally opt-in so it can be pointed at a real external REDAP deployment or public Hugging Face repo without making CI depend on a huge remote dataset.

The Hugging Face helper handles the missing entry point for `.rrd` datasets hosted on HF: it uses the HF dataset tree API, follows pagination, filters `.rrd` files, preserves subpaths, supports private/gated repos via token, and registers explicit raw URLs instead of requiring a local download.

The local REDAP HTTP loader intentionally requires range-capable RRDs with a footer. That keeps registration lazy: validation/enumeration reads the remote footer/manifest over HTTP ranges, and later queries either fetch selected chunks directly from the HTTP source or fall back to `FetchChunks`, which now understands the same direct RRD chunk keys.

Example measurement flow:

```bash
pixi run uvpy scripts/redap_scrub_metrics.py \
  --redap-url rerun+http://127.0.0.1:<port> \
  --dataset droid_sample \
  --index log_time \
  --hf-repo rerun/droid_sample \
  --hf-limit 20 \
  --seek-count 8 \
  --json
```

Live local-server smoke against `rerun/droid_sample` (`--hf-limit 3`, `--index log_time`, direct URLs enabled):

| query | segments | chunks | direct requests | direct bytes | gRPC bytes | rows | wall ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| full scan | 3 | 756 | 16 | 109,099,488 | 0 | 3,082 | 58,549 |
| seek 1 | 1 | 211 | 3 | 16,208,664 | 0 | 1 | 2,327 |
| seek 2 | 1 | 211 | 3 | 16,207,640 | 0 | 1 | 999 |
| seek 3 | 1 | 211 | 3 | 16,200,088 | 0 | 1 | 997 |

All three seeks had `filters_pushed_down=1`, `filters_applied_client_side=0`, `error_kind=null`, `fetch_direct_bytes == fetch_bytes`, and `fetch_grpc_bytes=0`.

Larger no-full-scan smoke against the same public HF repo (`--hf-limit 10`, `--seek-count 5`) also stayed bounded: each seek touched one segment, fetched ~16.2 MB via direct HTTP ranges, had `fetch_grpc_bytes=0`, and completed in ~0.9-2.6s wall time on this machine/network.

### Tests

- `cargo fmt --package re_datafusion`
- `cargo test -p re_datafusion --lib`
- `python -m py_compile scripts/redap_scrub_metrics.py rerun_py/tests/e2e_redap_tests/test_query_metrics_behaviors.py rerun_py/rerun_sdk/rerun/catalog/_entry.py rerun_py/tests/unit/test_catalog_huggingface.py`
- `pixi run ruff check scripts/redap_scrub_metrics.py rerun_py/tests/e2e_redap_tests/test_query_metrics_behaviors.py rerun_py/rerun_sdk/rerun/catalog/_entry.py rerun_py/tests/unit/test_catalog_huggingface.py`
- `pixi run uvpy -m pytest -c rerun_py/pyproject.toml rerun_py/tests/e2e_redap_tests/test_query_metrics_behaviors.py -q`
- `pixi run uvpy -m pytest -c rerun_py/pyproject.toml rerun_py/tests/unit/test_catalog_huggingface.py rerun_py/tests/e2e_redap_tests/test_query_metrics_behaviors.py::test_scrub_seeks_fetch_bounded_slices -q`
- `cargo fmt --package re_server`
- `cargo check -p re_server`
- `pixi run py-build`
- `pixi run rrpy -m pytest -q rerun_py/tests/unit/test_catalog_huggingface.py rerun_py/tests/e2e_redap_tests/test_query_metrics_behaviors.py::test_scrub_seeks_fetch_bounded_slices`
- Live resolver smoke: `_resolve_huggingface_rrd_urls("rerun/droid_sample", limit=3)` returned canonical HF `.rrd` URLs without downloading them.
- Live local REDAP smoke: `rr.server.Server()` registered `DatasetEntry.register_huggingface("rerun/droid_sample", limit=1)`, and `get_index_ranges()` returned `log_tick`, `log_time`, and `real_time` ranges.
- Live local REDAP direct metrics smoke: `scripts/redap_scrub_metrics.py --hf-repo rerun/droid_sample --hf-limit 3 --seek-count 3 --include-full-scan --json` produced the direct-fetch table above.
- Live local REDAP larger scrub smoke: `scripts/redap_scrub_metrics.py --hf-repo rerun/droid_sample --hf-limit 10 --seek-count 5 --json` kept all sampled seeks to one segment and direct HTTP ranges only.

Fixes part of #11315.

data.title: Load OBJ material sidecars in importer
data.body:
### Related

* Closes #3773
* Follows up #3772

### What

This PR makes native OBJ file imports resolve their Wavefront material sidecars instead of logging the OBJ bytes as a standalone `Asset3D` blob.

When an `.obj` file is opened through the importer, Rerun now:

* loads referenced `.mtl` files relative to the OBJ file,
* converts each OBJ model into native `Mesh3D` data,
* preserves positions, triangle indices, normals, and UV coordinates,
* maps MTL `Kd`/`d` values to `Mesh3D::albedo_factor`,
* decodes `map_Kd` diffuse textures and logs them as `Mesh3D` albedo textures.

This leaves non-OBJ mesh imports on the existing `Asset3D` path.

### Screenshot

Imported OBJ with its referenced MTL and PNG texture preserved:

![Imported textured OBJ in Rerun](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Reza2kn/rerun-codex-fork/codex/pr-assets/pr-assets/3773/color_ripple_obj_front_perspective_c_9576d31.png)

### Notes

#3772 fixed `.obj` media-type guessing. The remaining issue in #3773 was that an OBJ file loaded by itself has no access to its MTL/texture sidecars at render time. Resolving those sidecars in the native file importer lets the viewer receive complete `Mesh3D` archetypes with material data already attached.

### Validation

* `cargo fmt -p re_importer`
* `git diff --check`
* `cargo check -p re_importer`
* `cargo test -p re_importer --test test_obj_importer`
* `cargo test -p re_importer`

data.title: [codex] Add Rust blueprint view parity
data.body:
## What

Adds Rust SDK parity for Python blueprint view snippets and view configuration:

- generates typed Rust blueprint view wrappers from the view `.fbs` definitions
- adds Rust snippets for every `docs/snippets/all/views/*` Python snippet
- removes the Rust opt-out for view snippets and makes the snippet runner use full snippet paths
- makes the `spatial3d` and `tensor` snippets deterministic so RRD and visual regressions are stable
- adds viewer-level visual regression snapshots for all blueprint view snippets

Closes #5521.

## Why

The Rust SDK had manually maintained blueprint view wrappers and the docs/snippet coverage was Python-only for the view examples. That made it easy for Rust to drift behind Python and hard to prove parity.

This moves the view wrappers to schema-driven generation and adds both semantic RRD parity checks and pixel-level viewer coverage for the snippets.

data.title: Use color bar with vertically split proportion to indicate the percentage of states in a merged region.
data.body: ### Related * Closes #12829 ### What When a lane in the state timeline view has many state changes packed too tightly to render individually (narrower than 4px on screen), they're folded into a single merged region. Previously this merged region rendered as a flat, uniformly-colored box labeled "N states" — all information about which states were present, and for how long, was lost. This PR replaces that flat box with a duration-weighted stacked color chart: the merged region's screen width is split into fixed-width time buckets (~3px each, capped at 512 buckets), and each bucket is rendered as a small stacked column where every distinct state's color contributes a height proportional to the fraction of that bucket's time span it actually occupied. This lets a densely collapsed region still visually convey which state dominated a given interval, instead of hiding that information behind a generic gray box. Details: - The stacking order of colors within a bucket is sorted alphabetically by state label (rather than by first-seen order), so it stays stable across adjacent merged regions and while panning/zooming — first-seen order would otherwise cause the stack to visually flip depending on which phase happened to scroll into view first. - The "N states" label is no longer drawn on the region itself (it competed visually with the chart); the phase count is still available via the existing hover tooltip. - examples/rust/state_timeline_example now logs a densely-packed lane so the new rendering is visible by default without having to zoom into a tiny slice of the timeline. - Added/updated the state_timeline_merge_small_phases snapshot test to cover the new rendering. ## Screenshots **States when compactly folded** **States when zoomed in**

data.title: `RecordingStream` used as a context manager only persists the first row (regression in 0.32.0)

labels.name: 🪵 Log & send APIs
labels.description: Affects the user-facing API for all languages

data.body:
## Summary

When a `RecordingStream` is created and `.save()`d to a file, and then its context
manager (`with stream:`) is **re-entered once per logged frame**, only the data
from the **first** `with` block is written to the `.rrd`. Everything logged in
later `with` blocks is silently dropped.

Using the stream's methods directly (`stream.set_time(...)`, `stream.log(...)`),
or keeping a single `with` block open around the whole loop, persists everything.

This is a regression: it works on **0.31.4** and is broken from **0.32.0** onward
(still broken in 0.33.1). Nothing in the 0.32.x changelog documents a change to
`save()` / stream lifecycle, so this looks unintentional.

## Minimal reproducer

```python
import numpy as np
import rerun as rr

stream = rr.RecordingStream("repro")
stream.save("/tmp/repro.rrd")
for i in range(5):
    with stream:  # re-entering the context per frame drops all but frame 0
        rr.set_time("frame", sequence=i)
        rr.log("img", rr.Image(np.zeros((4, 4, 3), np.uint8)))
del stream
```

## How to run + inspect

```bash
# broken: rerun 0.33.1
uv run --isolated --with 'rerun-sdk==0.33.1' --with numpy python repro.py
uv run --isolated --with 'rerun-sdk==0.33.1' rerun rrd print --entity /img /tmp/repro.rrd

# works: rerun 0.31.4 (last good version)
uv run --isolated --with 'rerun-sdk==0.31.4' --with numpy python repro.py
uv run --isolated --with 'rerun-sdk==0.31.4' rerun rrd print --entity /img /tmp/repro.rrd
```

`rerun rrd print --entity /img` lists one `Chunk … - /img` line per persisted
frame, so the count of those lines is the number of frames that survived.

### Output — 0.31.4 (works): 5 frames

```
store_version: 0.31.4
Chunk(…2950cc5f85a8ea53) with 1 rows (1.2 KiB) - /img - data columns: [Image:buffer Image:format]
Chunk(…2950cc5f85a8ea54) with 1 rows (1.2 KiB) - /img - data columns: [Image:buffer Image:format]
Chunk(…2950cc5f85a8ea55) with 1 rows (1.2 KiB) - /img - data columns: [Image:buffer Image:format]
Chunk(…2950cc5f85a8ea56) with 1 rows (1.2 KiB) - /img - data columns: [Image:buffer Image:format]
Chunk(…2950cc5f85a8ea57) with 1 rows (1.2 KiB) - /img - data columns: [Image:buffer Image:format]
```

### Output — 0.33.1 (broken): 1 frame

```
store_version: 0.33.1
Chunk(…3ffe479e1330c4cf) with 1 rows (1.2 KiB) - /img - data columns: [Image:buffer Image:format]
```

data.title: Frame picker / browsable TF tree for the 3D view's "Target frame"
data.body: ### Motivation The MCAP tf parser logs every `/tf` / `/tf_static` transform to a single entity using explicit `parent_frame`/`child_frame` IDs, so the frame graph is fully decoupled from the entity-path tree — there's no way to **browse** it in the viewer. Robotics users coming from Foxglove expect a "TF tree" they can navigate. This shows up concretely at **Spatial information → Target frame** on a 3D view (`SpatialInformation.target_frame`): it's the view's display/anchor frame, but it's edited as a free-form text field — you have to already know the frame name to type it. ### Proposal Hang a **frame picker** off the existing `…` affordance on that row: a searchable, hierarchical tree of transform frames (modeled on the entity picker — `view_entity_picker.rs`: modal + search + `show_hierarchical_with_children`), sourced from the frame tree instead of `EntityTree`. Selecting a frame writes the `target_frame` blueprint override. The popup doubles as the browsable TF tree. _(screenshot below: current "Target frame" field, annotated with where the picker would go)_ ### Questions before I start 1. **Roadmap:** Is a frame tree-browser / picker already planned? The `re_tf` named-frames work looks recent and I'd rather not duplicate it. 2. **Scope:** Picker on `target_frame` only, or a reusable `TransformFrameId` editor (the per-entity `coordinate_frame_ui` autocomplete could share it)? 3. **API:** `TransformForest` exposes roots and a flattened `root_from_frame()`, but no parent→children adjacency. Reconstruct from per-frame `parent_frame`, or add a `children_of()`/edges accessor — preference? ### Screenshot

data.title: Web viewer catalog segment table does not refresh without manual reload
data.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When using the web viewer to display a catalog URL (e.g., `rerun+http://127.0.0.1:51234/catalog`), the segment table in the recording panel does not automatically or reactively update when new segments are registered server-side via e.g. `dataset.register().wait()`.

Currently, the only way to see newly registered segments is to manually reload the browser page.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
The web viewer needs a mechanism to refresh or synchronize the catalog segment table when new segments are registered server-side. Potential solutions could include:

1. **API-driven manual refresh:** Introduce a `refresh_catalog()` method in the web viewer API to programmatically force a re-fetch of catalog metadata.
2. **Connection management:** Ensure `viewer.close()` properly terminates and clears server connections (catalog URLs), as it currently only works for discrete data sources. A refresh could then by forced by calling `viewer.close()` + `viewer.open()`
3. **Reactive updates (Long-term):** Extend the REDAP protocol to support subscription-based catalog updates, allowing the viewer to automatically react to server-side segment registration notifications.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

* **Manual browser reload:** This is the only current workaround, but it requires manual user intervention and completely resets the application state.
* **Direct dataset/segment URLs:** Opening specific dataset/segment URLs directly instead of navigating via the catalog. While these individual segments can be opened and closed using their catalog URL, this still does not update the segments table.
* **Viewer lifecycle restart (`viewer.stop()` + `viewer.start()`):** Does not fetch the updated state.

data.title: rr_recording_stream_free blocks forever when connected to an unreachable gRPC endpoint after many log calls
data.body:
<!--
First look if there is already a similar bug report. If there is, upvote the issue with 👍
-->

---

### Description

**SDK version:** 0.33.0 (C/C++ API), Linux x86_64

`rr_recording_stream_free` never returns when the stream is connected to a gRPC endpoint that is not reachable, after a large number of `log` calls.

#### Steps to reproduce

1. `rr_recording_stream_new`
2. `rr_recording_stream_connect_grpc` to an endpoint that is not a reachable Rerun server, e.g. `rerun+http://app-rerun-viewer:8080/proxy` (returns immediately, no error).
3. Log ~1,000,000 Float64 scalars in a loop, each at its own `SEQUENCE` timeline point (`rr_recording_stream_set_time` + `rr_recording_stream_log`).
4. Call `rr_recording_stream_free(stream)`.

#### Observed behavior

`rr_recording_stream_free` does not return (verified by terminating with a watchdog after 60s).

#### Expected behavior

`rr_recording_stream_free` returns within a bounded time.

#### Additional data points

- With a single / small number of logged rows, `rr_recording_stream_free` returns after ~6s (gRPC "unable to connect" timeout).
- With 100,000 rows it returns; with 1,000,000 rows it hangs.
- Sending the same 1,000,000 rows via `rr_recording_stream_send_columns` instead of per-row `log` returns after ~6s and does not hang.

#### Script to reproduce C-API
```c
// Minimal working example demonstrating that `rr_recording_stream_free` blocks
// forever (despite its docstring claiming it does *not* block) when streaming
// data to a gRPC endpoint that never becomes a working Rerun server -- e.g. a
// service name like `app-rerun-viewer:8080` that does not resolve / is not a
// Rerun gRPC server.
//
// Observed behaviour (rerun 0.33):
//   * If only a *single* row is logged, `rr_recording_stream_free` returns
//     after ~6s. Bounded -- NO hang.
//   * If *many* rows are logged across many timeline points (one log() per
//     value per timeline sample), `rr_recording_stream_free` never returns.
//     THIS is the hang this program reproduces.
//   * The columnar `send_columns` path (3rd arg "columns") submits the same
//     number of logical rows in a single call. It does NOT hang:
//     `rr_recording_stream_free` returns after ~6s.
//
// The number of rows logged via the row API is what determines whether the
// hang occurs, not the byte size of any single row.
//
// Flow:
//   1. create a recording stream
//   2. connect_grpc to the endpoint (returns immediately, no error)
//   3. log NUM_ROWS scalars, each at its own timeline point
//   4. free the stream
//
// A SIGALRM watchdog fires after WATCHDOG_SECONDS so the program terminates and
// proves that `rr_recording_stream_free` never returned (exit code 42).
//
// Usage:
//   dev-rerun_free_hang                          # default hostname URL
//   dev-rerun_free_hang <rerun-grpc-url>         # point at any URL you want
//   dev-rerun_free_hang <rerun-grpc-url> <n>     # log <n> rows (default 100000)
//   dev-rerun_free_hang <rerun-grpc-url> <n> columns  # send <n> rows via the
//                                                     # columnar send_columns API

#include <rerun/c/rerun.h>

#include <signal.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <unistd.h>

#define WATCHDOG_SECONDS 60
#define DEFAULT_NUM_ROWS 100000

static void check(const rr_error* error, const char* what) {
    if (error->code != RR_ERROR_CODE_OK) {
        fprintf(stderr, "[mwe] %s failed (code=%u): %s\n", what, error->code, error->description);
        exit(1);
    }
}

// Arrow release callbacks. The data we hand over is static, so releasing only
// needs to mark the structures as released (set release = NULL).
static void release_schema(struct ArrowSchema* schema) {
    schema->release = NULL;
}
static void release_array(struct ArrowArray* array) {
    array->release = NULL;
}

static void on_watchdog(int signum) {
    (void)signum;
    static const char msg[] =
        "\n[mwe] WATCHDOG: rr_recording_stream_free() is STILL blocked after the "
        "timeout -> reproduced the hang. Killing process.\n";
    write(STDERR_FILENO, msg, sizeof(msg) - 1);
    _exit(42);
}

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    const char* url;
    long num_rows = DEFAULT_NUM_ROWS;
    int use_columns = 0;

    if (argc > 1) {
        url = argv[1];
    } else {
        url = "rerun+http://app-rerun-viewer:8080/proxy";
    }
    if (argc > 2) {
        num_rows = strtol(argv[2], NULL, 10);
    }
    if (argc > 3 && strcmp(argv[3], "columns") == 0) {
        use_columns = 1;
    }

    fprintf(stderr, "[mwe] rerun SDK version: %s\n", rr_version_string());
    fprintf(stderr, "[mwe] using gRPC URL: %s\n", url);
    fprintf(stderr, "[mwe] logging %ld rows via %s API\n", num_rows, use_columns ? "send_columns" : "row log");

    rr_error error = {0};

    // 1. Create the recording stream.
    const rr_store_info store_info = {
        .application_id = rr_make_string("rr_free_hang_mwe"),
        .recording_id = (rr_string){0},
        .store_kind = RR_STORE_KIND_RECORDING,
    };
    const rr_recording_stream stream = rr_recording_stream_new(&store_info, true, &error);
    check(&error, "rr_recording_stream_new");

    // 2. Connect to an unavailable gRPC endpoint. This returns immediately and
    //    only validates URL syntax, not reachability.
    rr_recording_stream_connect_grpc(stream, rr_make_string(url), &error);
    check(&error, "rr_recording_stream_connect_grpc");
    fprintf(stderr, "[mwe] connect_grpc returned (no connection error, as documented)\n");

    // 3. Log many Float64 scalars, each at its own timeline point. Logging via
    //    the C API requires Arrow FFI structs.
    struct ArrowSchema schema = {
        .format = "g", // Arrow format string for float64 (double)
        .name = "item",
        .metadata = NULL,
        .flags = 0,
        .n_children = 0,
        .children = NULL,
        .dictionary = NULL,
        .release = release_schema,
        .private_data = NULL,
    };
    const rr_component_type component_type = {
        .descriptor =
            {
                .archetype = rr_make_string("rerun.archetypes.Scalars"),
                .component = rr_make_string("Scalars:scalars"),
                .component_type = rr_make_string("rerun.components.Scalar"),
            },
        .schema = schema,
    };
    const rr_component_type_handle type_handle = rr_register_component_type(component_type, &error);
    check(&error, "rr_register_component_type");

    if (use_columns) {
        // 3b. Columnar path: build a single ListArray of all scalars plus a
        //     parallel i64 time column and hand them to send_columns. This
        //     submits the same number of logical rows as the row loop in one
        //     call.
        int32_t* offsets = malloc(sizeof(int32_t) * (size_t)(num_rows + 1));
        double* col_values = malloc(sizeof(double) * (size_t)num_rows);
        int64_t* time_values = malloc(sizeof(int64_t) * (size_t)num_rows);
        if (offsets == NULL || col_values == NULL || time_values == NULL) {
            fprintf(stderr, "[mwe] allocation failed for %ld rows\n", num_rows);
            exit(1);
        }
        for (long i = 0; i < num_rows; ++i) {
            offsets[i] = (int32_t)i;
            col_values[i] = (double)i;
            time_values[i] = i;
        }
        offsets[num_rows] = (int32_t)num_rows;

        // Child float64 values array of the ListArray.
        static const void* child_buffers[2];
        child_buffers[0] = NULL; // validity
        child_buffers[1] = col_values;
        static struct ArrowArray child_array;
        child_array = (struct ArrowArray){
            .length = num_rows,
            .null_count = 0,
            .offset = 0,
            .n_buffers = 2,
            .n_children = 0,
            .buffers = child_buffers,
            .children = NULL,
            .dictionary = NULL,
            .release = release_array,
            .private_data = NULL,
        };
        static struct ArrowArray* list_children[1];
        list_children[0] = &child_array;

        // Outer ListArray: one list element (a single scalar) per logical row.
        static const void* list_buffers[2];
        list_buffers[0] = NULL; // validity
        list_buffers[1] = offsets;
        struct ArrowArray list_array = {
            .length = num_rows,
            .null_count = 0,
            .offset = 0,
            .n_buffers = 2,
            .n_children = 1,
            .buffers = list_buffers,
            .children = list_children,
            .dictionary = NULL,
            .release = release_array,
            .private_data = NULL,
        };

        // Time column (i64 primitive array).
        static const void* time_buffers[2];
        time_buffers[0] = NULL; // validity
        time_buffers[1] = time_values;
        struct ArrowArray time_array = {
            .length = num_rows,
            .null_count = 0,
            .offset = 0,
            .n_buffers = 2,
            .n_children = 0,
            .buffers = time_buffers,
            .children = NULL,
            .dictionary = NULL,
            .release = release_array,
            .private_data = NULL,
        };

        rr_time_column time_column = {
            .timeline =
                {
                    .name = rr_make_string("step"),
                    .type = RR_TIME_TYPE_SEQUENCE,
                },
            .array = time_array,
            .sorting_status = RR_SORTING_STATUS_SORTED,
        };
        rr_component_column component_column = {
            .component_type = type_handle,
            .array = list_array,
        };
        rr_recording_stream_send_columns(
            stream, rr_make_string("scalar"), &time_column, 1, &component_column, 1, &error);
        check(&error, "rr_recording_stream_send_columns");
        fprintf(stderr, "[mwe] sent %ld rows via send_columns\n", num_rows);
    } else {
        // 3a. Row path: log many Float64 scalars, each at its own timeline
        //     point.
        static double values[1] = {42.0};
        const void* buffers[2] = {NULL /* validity bitmap */, values};
        struct ArrowArray array = {
            .length = 1,
            .null_count = 0,
            .offset = 0,
            .n_buffers = 2,
            .n_children = 0,
            .buffers = buffers,
            .children = NULL,
            .dictionary = NULL,
            .release = release_array,
            .private_data = NULL,
        };
        rr_component_batch batch = {
            .component_type = type_handle,
            .array = array,
        };
        rr_data_row data_row = {
            .entity_path = rr_make_string("scalar"),
            .num_component_batches = 1,
            .component_batches = &batch,
        };

        for (long i = 0; i < num_rows; ++i) {
            values[0] = (double)i;
            rr_recording_stream_set_time(
                stream, rr_make_string("step"), RR_TIME_TYPE_SEQUENCE, i, &error);
            check(&error, "rr_recording_stream_set_time");
            // The Arrow array was "released" by the previous log call; re-arm it.
            array.release = release_array;
            batch.array = array;
            data_row.component_batches = &batch;
            rr_recording_stream_log(stream, data_row, true, &error);
            check(&error, "rr_recording_stream_log");
        }
        fprintf(stderr, "[mwe] logged %ld scalars\n", num_rows);
    }

    // 4. Arm the watchdog and free the stream. Per the docstring this should
    //    flush-but-not-block; in practice it blocks forever.
    signal(SIGALRM, on_watchdog);
    alarm(WATCHDOG_SECONDS);

    const time_t t0 = time(NULL);
    fprintf(stderr,
            "[mwe] calling rr_recording_stream_free() (watchdog: %d s)...\n",
            WATCHDOG_SECONDS);
    rr_recording_stream_free(stream);
    const time_t t1 = time(NULL);

    alarm(0);
    fprintf(stderr,
            "[mwe] rr_recording_stream_free() RETURNED after %ld s (no hang)\n",
            (long)(t1 - t0));
    return 0;
}


```

data.body: **Describe the bug** We have periods of time where video is not being recorded. I would like to "Clear" the video stream and have the frame show up as blank. I have tried several approaches to clearing this and none of them result in the desired behavior. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: ```python from __future__ import annotations import av import numpy as np import rerun as rr W, H = 320, 240 N_FRAMES = 30 def _h264_encoder(): """Open an all-intra H.264 encoder with the same settings used elsewhere.""" container = av.open("/dev/null", "w", format="h264") stream = container.add_stream("libx264", rate=30) stream.width = W stream.height = H stream.pix_fmt = "yuv420p" stream.max_b_frames = 0 stream.options = { "preset": "ultrafast", "crf": "30", "g": "1", "x264-params": "scenecut=0", } return container, stream def encode_h264_all_intra(band_color: tuple[int, int, int]) -> list[bytes]: """Encode `N_FRAMES` H.264 I-frames; one packet per frame.""" container, stream = _h264_encoder() out: list[bytes] = [] try: for i in range(N_FRAMES): arr = np.full((H, W, 3), 32, dtype=np.uint8) # dark grey background band_x = int((i / N_FRAMES) * W) arr[:, band_x : band_x + 24] = band_color frame = av.VideoFrame.from_ndarray(arr, format="rgb24").reformat(format="yuv420p") for pkt in stream.encode(frame): out.append(bytes(pkt)) for pkt in stream.encode(None): out.append(bytes(pkt)) finally: container.close() return out rr.init("rerun_example_video_stream_clear", spawn=True) ENTITIES = ["/baseline", "/clear", "/empty_sample", "/empty_codec"] # Anchor the codec at step 0 (non-static) on every entity, before any samples. rr.set_time("step", sequence=0) for entity in ENTITIES: rr.log(entity, rr.VideoStream.from_fields(codec=rr.components.VideoCodec.H264)) packets_red = encode_h264_all_intra(band_color=(220, 60, 60)) packets_green = encode_h264_all_intra(band_color=(60, 220, 60)) # Burst A (red) starts at step 10 (not 0) so we can see what the viewer renders # *before* any sample is logged — useful baseline for the "blanking" attempts. BURST_A_START = 10 for i, pkt in enumerate(packets_red): rr.set_time("step", sequence=BURST_A_START + i) for entity in ENTITIES: rr.log(entity, rr.VideoStream.from_fields(sample=pkt)) # At step 40, do nothing on /baseline. Then apply each attempt to its entity: rr.set_time("step", sequence=40) rr.log("/clear", rr.Clear(recursive=True)) rr.log("/empty_sample", rr.VideoStream.from_fields(sample=[])) rr.log("/empty_codec", rr.VideoStream.from_fields(codec=[])) # Burst B (green) on every entity at steps 60..89. for i, pkt in enumerate(packets_green): rr.set_time("step", sequence=60 + i) for entity in ENTITIES: rr.log(entity, rr.VideoStream.from_fields(sample=pkt)) ``` **Expected behavior** After rr.Clear(), the last frame of the video should no longer be visible., **Screenshots** **Rerun version** 0.32

data.title: WebGPU broken on Safari again – 3D viewport fails to render on Safari 26.4

labels.name: 🕸️ web
labels.description: regarding running the viewer in a browser

data.body: The web viewer's 3D viewport renders black on Safari 26.4 (macOS 26 Tahoe and iPadOS 26.4) when WebGPU is the active backend. Other view types (2D, time series, dataframe, etc.) render correctly. Switching to WebGL via "Restart with WebGL" in the viewer menu restores 3D rendering. This is a regression in Safari 26.4 specifically – Safari 26.3 on iOS still renders 3D correctly under WebGPU. Per [caniuse](https://caniuse.com/webgpu), Safari 26.x is still classified as "Partial support" for WebGPU. ### Steps to reproduce 1. On macOS 26.4 Tahoe or iPadOS 26.4 with Safari 26.4, open https://rerun.io/viewer in a new private window. 2. From the welcome screen, open any 3D example (e.g. "URDF"). **Expected:** the 3D viewport renders normally (as it does on Chrome, Firefox, Safari 26.3, and older Safari versions which use WebGL). **Actual:** the 3D viewport is black. No error toast or console errors are surfaced. The rest of the viewer UI renders correctly. ### Workaround In the viewer menu, click "Restart with WebGL". The viewer reloads with WebGL and 3D content renders correctly. ### Tested versions | OS | Safari | Result | |---|---|---| | macOS 26.4.1 Tahoe | 26.4 (21624.1.16.11.4) | ❌ 3D black | | iPadOS 26.4.2 | 26.4 | ❌ 3D black | | iOS 26.3.1 | 26.3 | ✅ works | | macOS 15.7.4 Sequoia | 18.6 | ✅ works (defaults to WebGL) | ### Mitigation in progress Reverting the default backend to WebGL on Safari while this is broken. Once Apple ships a Safari update that fixes 3D rendering under WebGPU, we can re-enable the WebGPU default. ### Related - #10609 – the predecessor: enabling WebGPU on Safari Tahoe in the first place. That worked on the Safari versions tested at the time; Safari 26.4 has subsequently regressed the 3D pipeline.

data.title: Panel toggle buttons should not be disabled when panel state overrides are set
data.body:
### Problem                                                                                     
                                                                  
  When the web viewer is embedded (e.g. [arkit](https://rerun.io/examples#spatial-computing/arkit_scenes)), the host page calls `override_panel_state()` to hide panels for a clean initial look in the context of web. This correctly hides the panels, but also **disables the toggle buttons** — making it impossible for users to open them without entering fullscreen first.

  The override API conflates two concerns:                                                    
  1. Setting the panel's visible state (intended)
  2. Disabling user interaction with the toggle button (unintended)                           


### Root cause                                                                                  
   
  In `top_panel.rs`, the panel toggle buttons use `*_overridden()` as a disable condition (for all three panels):        
                                                                  
```  
ui.add_enabled_ui(                                                                          
      route.has_selection_panel() && !app_blueprint.selection_panel_overridden(),
      ...                                                                                     
  ); 
```
When an override exists, the button is grayed out, the toggle action is also blocked through hot keys. 

### Proposed fix after chatting to claude

  - `top_panel.rs`: Remove `!app_blueprint.*_panel_overridden()` from the three `add_enabled_ui` conditions
  - `app_blueprint.rs`: Remove the early returns in `toggle_*_panel()` so clicking the button works, and toggle from the effective state (`self.*_panel_state()`) rather than the blueprint store value (`self.panel_states.*`)
  - Clear the override for that panel on toggle so it doesn't fight back on the next frame (?)

data.title: SDK: Inconsistent API behaviour logging / viewing data
data.body:
I started a Jupyter notebook to try and ingest and visualize some data.

# Logging to memory

Initially I log some data. Note how this logs to memory.

```python
import os
import numpy as np
import rerun as rr
import rerun.blueprint as rrb
from rerun.notebook import Viewer

with rr.RecordingStream("my-demo", recording_id="demo-1") as rec:
    n = 1000
    positions = np.random.rand(n, 3) * 10
    colors = np.random.randint(0, 255, size=(n, 3), dtype=np.uint8)

    for t in range(50):
        rec.set_time("frame", sequence=t)
        drift = positions + np.array([t * 0.05, 0, 0])
        rec.log("points", rr.Points3D(drift, colors=colors, radii=0.05))

    rec.flush()
    rec.disconnect()
```

Following this, visualising `rec` to works.

```python3
Viewer(width=800, height=500, recording=rec).display()
```

# Unexpected behaviour: Viewer does not load when logging to a file

If instead I log to a file with the same code, but editing the start of the `with` block to read:

```python
rrd_path = "/tmp/my-demo.rrd"
with rr.RecordingStream("my-demo", recording_id="demo-1") as rec:
    rec.save(rrd_path)

    # rest of the code is verbatim

Viewer(width=800, height=500, recording=rec).display()
```

The viewer loads with no data and no errors.

# Workaround

The current workaround is to load the recording again into separate objects:

```python
from rerun.recording import load_recording
recording = load_recording(rrd_path)
rec_view = rr.RecordingStream("my-demo-view", recording_id="view-1")
rec_view.send_recording(recording)
Viewer(width=800, height=500, recording=rec_view).display()
```

# Expected behaviour

I would expect the data to load up in the viewer, or at least error out with a meaningful message if the file recording stream is write-only while the memory one has an additional read cursor too.

When working interactively (read "playing around with data"), I think it would be useful to be able to visualise a recording before taking more actions with it, such as saving it to a server.

data.title: c++: arrow + latest macos issue
data.body:
I updated macOS and/or Xcode (not sure which one is at fault) and now I cannot use rerun with CMake's FetchContent.

The issue is that arrow tries to identify which `libtool` is in the PATH because they don't support gcc's one (or something like that). But the new `libtool` returns the version in a different format and their (old) regexp does not match anymore, so they error out.

The issue is fixed in arrow https://github.com/apache/arrow/pull/49370 

I think it's available in arrow version 24. Is it possible to update to the latest arrow (probably too early, it was just released), or can this patch be applied as part of the FetchContent-based setup? 


```diff
diff --git a/cpp/cmake_modules/BuildUtils.cmake b/cpp/cmake_modules/BuildUtils.cmake
index 692efa7..4f8f5e7 100644
--- a/cpp/cmake_modules/BuildUtils.cmake
+++ b/cpp/cmake_modules/BuildUtils.cmake
@@ -112,7 +112,7 @@ function(arrow_create_merged_static_lib output_target)
     execute_process(COMMAND ${LIBTOOL_MACOS} -V
                     OUTPUT_VARIABLE LIBTOOL_V_OUTPUT
                     OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE)
-    if(NOT "${LIBTOOL_V_OUTPUT}" MATCHES ".*cctools-([0-9.]+).*")
+    if(NOT "${LIBTOOL_V_OUTPUT}" MATCHES ".*cctools.+([0-9.]+).*")
       message(FATAL_ERROR "libtool found appears to be the incompatible GNU libtool: ${LIBTOOL_MACOS}"
       )
     endif()
```

data.title: Will C++ SDK Add load/read/query/open_rrd APIs ?
data.body:
Currently, the C++ SDK only supports logging/sending data (`log`, `save`, `spawn`, `connect`), but lacks any APIs to:
- Load/parse `.rrd` files
- Read/query previously logged data
- Open and inspect recordings from within C++

This makes it impossible to implement full data pipelines (capture → save → load → analyze) entirely in C++. Many robotics, real-time, and native applications need to both log and read back Rerun data without switching to Python/Rust.

If you are asking a question, use [the Rerun Discord server](https://discord.gg/PXtCgFBSmH) instead.

data.title: Improve text log view performance with cached indexing and virtualized rendering
data.body:
### Related

- No linked issue yet.

### What

Improve text log view performance for large numbers of log entries by replacing the eager per-frame expansion path with a cached, virtualized one.

Previously, the text log view eagerly expanded all matching `TextLog` data into a flat in-memory list, sorted the entire list, recalculated row heights from full text bodies, and rendered through the old heterogeneous row path. That approach works for small recordings, but it becomes expensive when a recording contains many log rows or large multi-line messages.

This PR introduces a store-level `TextLogCache` plus a per-view `TextLogProjectionState` so the view can work from lightweight row metadata instead of eagerly materializing every visible row body on every frame.

Main changes:
- Add `TextLogCache`, which indexes text-log chunks once and stores lightweight per-row metadata:
  - row id / instance id
  - timepoint
  - log level
  - color
  - explicit line count
  
- Support incremental append-only updates in the cache, while falling back to a rebuild for non-additive store edits.

- Add a per-view projection that:
  - tracks the currently included entities and active timeline
  - preserves the legacy stable row ordering
  - applies log-level filtering over cached row handles
  - caches prefix sums for multi-line row heights
  - reuses cached discovered levels for blueprint fallback UI
  
- Switch rendering to `egui_table` with a table delegate that:
  - resolves text bodies lazily for visible rows only
  - uses cached prefix sums for row positioning
  - preserves current-time autoscroll behavior
  - preserves current-time marker rendering
  
- Simplify `TextLogSystem` so it remains responsible for discoverability of `TextLog` entities, while the view owns cached loading/projection logic.

- Add unit tests covering:
  - sparse carry-forward behavior for level/color metadata
  - lazy body resolution from indexed chunks
  - additive vs non-additive cache revisions
  - explicit newline counting
  - filtered projection prefix sums
  - sorted merge behavior
  - scroll target behavior
  - current-time marker placement

This is intended to preserve existing user-visible behavior while making large text-log views much more responsive.

Local validation:
- `cargo check -p re_view_text_log`
- `cargo test -p re_view_text_log`

Both passed locally.

Breaking changes:

data.body:
<!--
Thank you for filing a pull request! We kindly ask you to:

1. Fill out this pull request template below, to make the review smoother.
2. Enable edits to your branch by our maintainers. This helps us to get your branch ready to merge. See here for more details:

-->

### Related

* Closes [#1234](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/10090)



### What

<!--
Make sure the PR title and labels are set to maximize their usefulness for the CHANGELOG,
and our `git log`.

If you have noticed any breaking changes, include them in the migration guide.

We track various metrics at <https://build.rerun.io>.

For maintainers:
* To run all checks from `main`, comment on the PR with `@rerun-bot full-check`.
* To deploy documentation changes immediately after merging this PR, add the `deploy docs` label.

For more details check the PR section on <https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md>.
-->

Adds B-frame support for H.264/H.265 streams on the `VideoStream` archetype.

#### New types:

`VideoPresentationTimestampOffset` datatype (transparent i64) and matching component — represents the per-sample offset from decode timestamp (DTS) to presentation timestamp (PTS), in timeline units.

#### Archetype changes (`VideoStream`):

`sample` field is now array-typed `VideoSample`, allowing multiple frames to be batched into a single row in decode order.

New optional `presentation_time_offset` field `VideoPresentationTimestampOffset — when present, PTS for sample i = DTS_i + offset_i. When absent, PTS == DTS (the common no-B-frame case, fully backward compatible).

#### Cache/decoder pipeline (`VideoStreamCache`):

Frame numbers are now assigned by presentation order (PTS-sorted) instead of decode order.
Sample durations are computed from PTS-sorted timestamps so scrubbing and seek work correctly.

read_pts_offsets_from_chunk extracts offset arrays from incoming chunks.

Incremental chunk additions properly update frame numbers and SamplesStatistics.
demux/mod.rs: video duration is now computed from actual min/max PTS to handle reordered frames.

data.title: Unify `SeriesLines` and `SeriesPoints` into a single visualizer
data.body:
## Summary
Currently, time series plots have two separate visualizers:

`SeriesLines` — draws lines (color, width, interpolation, aggregation)
`SeriesPoints` — draws scatter points (marker shape, marker size, color)
To show both lines and markers on the same entity, users must activate both visualizers — which is unintuitive and depends on multi-visualizer UX that isn't well-surfaced today.

### Proposal
Unify into a single `SeriesPlot` (or Series) visualizer with a style enum:

```
PlotStyle::Lines      — current SeriesLines behavior
PlotStyle::Points     — current SeriesPoints behavior  
PlotStyle::Both       — lines with data point markers
``` 

This would:

- Eliminate the conceptual split between "line series" and "point series"
- Make "show markers on my lines" a natural per-entity property instead of requiring multi-visualizer composition
- Allow `PointsDisplay` (currently a view-level toggle on `PlotInteraction`) to migrate to a per-entity setting
- Simplify the Python/Rust/C++ SDK API surface

Context: 
This came up while adding `PlotInteraction` blueprint archetype (#1123, #1164). The "always show markers" feature (PointsDisplay) is currently a view-wide toggle because adding it to `SeriesLines` would blur the boundary with `SeriesPoints` A unified visualizer resolves this tension cleanly.

The unified visualizer would accept both `SeriesLines` and `SeriesPoints` archetype inputs for backwards compatibility.

data.title: [WIP] Custom shader support for Mesh3D
data.body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8face5d0-70b8-4ba0-be3b-8fcf036a80a0

Feel free to ignore or close this as a slop PR.  I am exploring adding an API which we frequently need, which is the ability to represent more complex volumetric data natively via raymarching.   Given how scary volume raymarching can be, I figured it made more sense to attempt to add WGSL shader injection for Mesh3D's, so the Python client can handle the custom trickiness.

This should be flexible enough to handle the terrain example and much more, but not quite enough for Gaussian Splatting or Marching Cubes.  Ideally, someday there would be a Slang integration for multipass compute pipelines (which _could_ handle GS and MC), but, for now, I figured this would enable >50% of custom visualizer needs.

While the code is all vibed, the ergonomics might be useful to frame future discussions on high-expressiveness/low-effort multi-language extensibility.

## Summary

This PR adds **custom WGSL fragment shaders on Mesh3D entities**, enabling effects like volumetric raymarching, stylized rendering, and data-driven visualization. The end-to-end pipeline is fully functional: custom shaders render correctly with dynamic uniform/texture bindings resolved from the entity store.

### What's included

**Type system & SDK:**
- New components (`unstable`): `ShaderSource` (inline WGSL code) and `ShaderParameters` (JSON metadata describing uniform/texture bindings and their source entity paths)
- Updated `Mesh3D` archetype with two new optional fields across Rust, Python, and C++
- Python SDK: `Mesh3D` accepts `shader_source`/`shader_parameters` kwargs; `slang_utils.py` helper for compiling Slang to WGSL

**Renderer infrastructure:**
- Inline WGSL shader modules with content-hash caching in the shader module pool
- 3D texture manager (`GpuTexture3D` / `TextureManager3D`) for volumetric data, following the existing `GpuTexture2D` pattern
- `CustomShaderMeshRenderer` — dynamic render pipeline that reuses the standard mesh vertex stage (`instanced_mesh.wgsl`) with user-provided fragment shaders
- Custom bind group builder for dynamic uniform buffers + 3D texture bindings

**Parameter binding:**
- JSON-driven reflection metadata maps shader uniforms to named entity paths (relative or absolute)
- Uniform buffer packing with std140 layout (float, vec2, vec3, vec4, mat4)
- `Tensor` → `GpuTexture3D` conversion for volumetric data
- Graceful handling of streaming data: rendering is skipped when required bindings aren't yet available, retrying each frame

**Vertex shader extensions:**
- Added `position_object` and `camera_pos_object` to `VertexOut` — enables custom fragment shaders to do object-space raymarching without exceeding the GPU inter-stage component limit (31 max)
- `camera_pos_object` is computed in the vertex shader via adjugate inverse of the 3x3 rotation portion of `world_from_mesh`, using only 3 inter-stage scalar components instead of the 12 that passing the full matrix would require

**DICOM volumetric example:**
- Updated `dicom_mri.py` with a raymarched volumetric rendering alongside the existing tensor view
- Logs a `[0,1]³` unit-cube mesh with a custom WGSL fragment shader that raymarches through a 3D volume texture
- Volume data logged as a downscaled 3D `Tensor` (≤128 per dimension) bound to the shader via entity path reference
- Shader parameters (`density_scale`, `value_range`) logged as `Scalars`/`Tensor` and resolved dynamically at each frame

### Architecture

```
SDK side (Python):                         Viewer side (Rust):
  slangpy compiles .slang → WGSL             Receives WGSL source + reflection JSON
  slangpy reflects params → JSON             Builds dynamic bind group from reflection
  rr.log("mesh", Mesh3D(                    Creates dynamic render pipeline
    ...,                                     Queries referenced entity data at current time
    shader_source=wgsl_str,                  Uploads uniforms/textures to GPU
    shader_parameters=json_str,              Renders with custom fragment shader
  ))
```

### Key files

| Area | Files |
|------|-------|
| Type definitions | `shader_source.fbs`, `shader_parameters.fbs`, `mesh3d.fbs` |
| Renderer infra | `custom_shader_mesh.rs`, `texture_manager_3d.rs`, `shader_module_pool.rs` |
| Parameter binding | `shader_params.rs`, `shader_param_resolver.rs`, `custom_shader_bind_group.rs` |
| Visualizer | `meshes.rs` (extended with shader component queries) |
| Vertex shader | `instanced_mesh.wgsl` (added `position_object`, `camera_pos_object`) |
| Python | `mesh3d_ext.py`, `slang_utils.py` |
| Example | `dicom_mri.py`, `volume_raymarch.wgsl`, `volume_raymarch.slang` |

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo clippy` passes on `re_renderer`, `re_view_spatial`, `re_sdk_types`
- [x] `cargo test -p re_sdk_types` — Mesh3D roundtrip test passes with new fields
- [x] `cargo test -p re_renderer` — all tests pass
- [x] `cargo test -p re_view_spatial` — all tests pass (including shader_params tests)
- [x] `cargo fmt` clean
- [x] `ruff` clean on Python files
- [x] End-to-end manual testing: DICOM volumetric raymarching renders correctly with dynamic parameter binding
- [x] Texture streaming race condition handled gracefully (skips rendering until data arrives)
- [ ] Snapshot regression tests for default Mesh3D rendering (unchanged behavior)
- [ ] CI validation (pending)

data.title: Add Android viewer with hardware-accelerated H.264/H.265 video decoding
data.body:
## Summary

This PR adds a native Android port of the Rerun Viewer with hardware-accelerated H.264 and H.265 video decoding via Android's MediaCodec API.

### What's included

**Android Viewer Application** (`crates/viewer/re_viewer_android/`)
- Full Gradle project that packages the Rerun Viewer as an Android APK
- `RerunActivity` (GameActivity-based) entry point with touch input normalization
- `android_main()` Rust entry point that spawns a gRPC server, configures eframe/egui with Vulkan/wgpu, and launches the standard Rerun `App`
- Touch-friendly egui style adjustments (larger hit targets, wider scrollbars)
- Minimum API 28 (Android 9), targeting API 35

**Hardware Video Decoding** (`crates/utils/re_video/src/decode/`)
- `android_mediacodec.rs`: `MediaCodecDecoder` implementing `SyncDecoder` for H.264 (AVC) and H.265 (HEVC)
- `ndk_media_codec.rs`: Hand-rolled minimal FFI bindings to the NDK `AMediaCodec` / `AMediaFormat` C API (~20 functions, avoiding the weight of `ndk-sys`)
- NV12/I420 to planar YUV420 pixel format conversion with stride handling
- Wired into the decoder factory in `decode/mod.rs` with a `with_mediacodec` cfg alias (Android-only)

**Platform Guards & Compatibility**
- `desktop` cfg alias (`all(not(wasm32), not(android))`) to simplify repeated platform checks in `app.rs`
- `rfd` (file dialog) and `re_tracing` server feature conditionally excluded from Android builds
- File dialog, profiler, and Docker detection gracefully disabled on Android
- `cfg_aliases` added to `re_viewer/build.rs` and `re_video/build.rs`

**CI**
- `.github/workflows/reusable_build_android.yml`: Reusable workflow that builds the Rust library for arm64-v8a + x86_64 and produces debug/release APKs

**Other**
- `android_logger` added to workspace dependencies
- `build-android` pixi task for local development
- `re_viewer_android` excluded from the Cargo workspace (built separately via `cargo-ndk`)

### How to build

See [`crates/viewer/re_viewer_android/README.md`](crates/viewer/re_viewer_android/README.md) for full instructions. Quick version:

```sh
# 1. Build native library
cargo ndk -t arm64-v8a -t x86_64 \
  -o crates/viewer/re_viewer_android/app/src/main/jniLibs \
  build --release -p re_viewer --lib --features android-game-activity

# 2. Build APK
cd crates/viewer/re_viewer_android && ./gradlew assembleDebug

# 3. Install
adb install app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
```

data.title: Improve Python logging performance of small things like `Transform3D`
data.body: ## Related * https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/12485 * https://github.com/rerun-io/reality/pull/184 ## What When logging many small things, e.g. transforms, the overhead of each log call can be significant, and on the order of 40µs. That's 20x slower than Rust. ## Why Generated with the instructions in `rerun/tests/python/log_benchmark/test_log_benchmark.py` ### Culprit 1: arrow encoding A lot of that overhead is from encoding the data into arrow, which is done in Python using py-arrow. We're essentially generating a bunch of single-row columns - something Arrow is _not_ optimized for. There are a few plausible avenues to explore: * Batch many `rr.log` call _in Python_ so we can encode them all at once. * Use codegen to generate more efficient arrow encoding code than what pyarrow provides * Switch from arrow to something else for the Python->Rust interface ### Culprit 2: `_log_components` overhead I'm not sure what we can do here, except to batch `rr.log` calls in Python. The problem then becomes when and how to flush those calls. ## Workaround: manual batching Batch many small `rr.log` call into one big one. Most of our archetypes support logging many at once (e.g. log many points at once instead of a single one).
