data.title: Hover, segmentation and pan/zoom support for rr.Tensor
data.body: ### Related * Closes #4307 * Closes #6849 * Closes #12010 ### What This PR introduces quality of life improvements to rr.Tensor that have been requested multiple times. Note that I do not know much rust, so a lot of this code was crafted with help from agents. I understand that the maintainers are busy and have little bandwidth to review, but I figured I'd open this PR since the features are working, and if someone with better knowledge wants to take this on or do some testing so these features can make it into main, they might as well have a starting point. Some things that would have to be done before merging are probably documentation and fallback cases. Currently the segmentation will not show without an AnnotationContext, which can be confusing. The hover UI could also be cleaned up a bit. Summary - Add segmentation-mask support for tensors with overlay opacity. - this is done by passing multiple tensors into a single TensorView. - Introduce rr.Tensor hover UI in line with rr.Image (zoom preview, pixel values/labels). - Improve tensor interaction (wheel slice scroll, pan/zoom, reset). In the screenshot below, note the hover UI and the controllable opacity for the segmentation overlay. Here an MWE: ```python import rerun as rr import numpy as np import rerun.blueprint as rrb def main(): rr.init("segmentation_overlay_test", spawn=True) # 1. Define the Annotation Context # This defines how the integer labels in the segmentation tensor are colored. rr.log("/", rr.AnnotationContext([ rr.AnnotationInfo(id=0, label="Background", color=(0, 0, 0)), rr.AnnotationInfo(id=1, label="Brain Tissue", color=(255, 100, 100)), # Opaque red rr.AnnotationInfo(id=2, label="Ventricles", color=(100, 100, 255)), # Opaque blue ]), static=True) # 2. Create synthetic 3D data (Z, Y, X) shape = (32, 128, 128) z, y, x = np.ogrid[:shape[0], :shape[1], :shape[2]] # Base MRI: A fuzzy sphere dist_sq = (x - 64)**2 + (y - 64)**2 + (z - 16)**2 mri = np.exp(-dist_sq / (2 * 40**2)).astype(np.float32) mri += np.random.normal(0, 0.05, shape) # Add noise # Segmentation: Integer labels seg = np.zeros(shape, dtype=np.uint16) seg[dist_sq < 45**2] = 1 # Brain seg[dist_sq < 15**2] = 2 # Ventricles # 3. Log the tensors # We name the dimensions so the Tensor View can map them correctly dim_names = ["z", "y", "x"] rr.log("volume/mri", rr.Tensor(mri, dim_names=dim_names)) rr.log("volume/segmentation", rr.Tensor(seg, dim_names=dim_names, opacity=0.5)) # 4. Set up a Blueprint to show both in the same Tensor View # My changes allow the TensorView to consume multiple entities. blueprint = rrb.Blueprint( rrb.TensorView( name="Slicer Overlay", origin="volume", contents=["volume/mri", "volume/segmentation"] ) ) rr.send_blueprint(blueprint) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```

data.title: `.serve_grpc()` should be possible to use independently of recording stream
data.body:
In the Python SDK, the only way to spawn an internal grpc_server is using the `.serve_grpc()` APIs.

The grpc server is stored in a LogSink and is automatically cleaned up if the corresponding recording goes out of scope or is disconnected.

This leads to confusing situations like the following:
```python
import rerun as rr

rr.init("rerun_example_grpc_server")

# Create a grpc server
uri = rr.serve_grpc()

# A user might want to connect to it with a dedicated stream
rec1 = rr.RecordingStream("rerun_example_grpc_server")
rec1.connect_grpc(uri)
rec1.log("object_stream", rr.TextLog("This works"))

# Later they set up the global recording to go to file isntead
rr.save("rerun_example_grpc_server.rerun")

# Doing the same thing, now fail because the grpc server was implicitly shut down
# when the global recording was switched to a file sin
rec2 = rr.RecordingStream("rerun_example_grpc_server")
rec2.connect_grpc(uri)
rec2.log("object_stream", rr.TextLog("This fail"))
```

It would be nice if a dedicated server object was created, separate of the stream concepts:
```python
import rerun as rr

# Create a grpc server. As long as the server object exists
server = rr.GrpcServer()

# A user can then connect to the server with a stream
rec1 = rr.RecordingStream("rerun_example_grpc_server")
rec1.connect_grpc(server)
rec1.log("object_stream", rr.TextLog("This works"))

# Changes to the global stream have no implicit impact on the server object
rr.save("rerun_example_grpc_server.rerun")

# A user can still connect and log to the server
rec2 = rr.RecordingStream("rerun_example_grpc_server")
rec2.connect_grpc(server)
rec2.log("object_stream", rr.TextLog("This still works"))
```

data.title: Add support for free-threaded python
data.body:
**Describe the bug**

I've been using rerun in one of my projects for quite a while now, and it's been working perfectly fine. We've hit some pretty intense compute bottlenecks, and we're now switching to using free-threaded python to bypass the GIL. Python itself and pip are working just fine:

```shell
$ python -VV
Python 3.14.2 free-threading build (main, Dec  9 2025, 19:03:17) [Clang 21.1.4 ]
$ pip -VV
pip 25.3 from XXX/.venv/lib/python3.14t/site-packages/pip (python 3.14)
```

But for some reason I cannot `pip install rerun-sdk`, as it's just not finding the package. Note that this works perfectly fine if I use normal `python 3.14`, but using `3.14t`  breaks. It's definitely not a versioning issue, as I'm also using the same versions of everything.

```shell
$ pip install rerun-sdk
ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement rerun-sdk (from versions: none)
ERROR: No matching distribution found for rerun-sdk

# this is the commit for 0.27.3
$ pip install --pre --no-index -f https://build.rerun.io/commit/3bddb14/wheels rerun-sdk
Looking in links: https://build.rerun.io/commit/3bddb14/wheels
ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement rerun-sdk (from versions: none)
ERROR: No matching distribution found for rerun-sdk
```

**To Reproduce**

1. Install free-threaded python.
2. Attempt to `pip install` the SDK, either using the package name, or from the wheels.

**Expected behavior**

The package gets installed.

**Screenshots**

N/A

**Backtrace**

N/A

**Desktop (please complete the following information):**

 - Arch: x64

**Original Post**

https://discord.com/channels/1062300748202921994/1451075642824069251

**Additional context**

To me it looks like a compatibility issue, where the wheels that are being built aren't compatible with CPython. This might be because of the [ABI](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/specifications/platform-compatibility-tags/#use) - your releases are for `-abi3` where my python only supports `-none`, ~~or it could be because you are targeting python `3.10` not `3.14`~~.

data.title: Make it easy to extract typed rerun components for .rrd recordings
data.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
reconstructing a typed rr.Image / rr.Pinhole / rr.Point3d from a .rrd file requires too many lines of the code. That is, after querying an .rrd file (load_recording -> view -> select -> read_all), there's not a simple way to deserialize the columnar format into an iterable set of rows of the original type. Here's an example of recreating an rr.Image - the least complicated of all

```def iter_color_frames(rrd_path: str):
    rrd = rr.dataframe.load_recording(rrd_path)
    timeline="frame"
    path="/camera/0/color/image"
    view = rrd.view(index=timeline, contents=path)
    table = view.select().read_all()
    frame_col = table[timeline]
    buf_col_name = f"{path}:Image:buffer"
    buf_col   = table[buf_col_name]
    fmt_col_name = f"{path}:Image:format"
    fmt_col   = table[fmt_col_name]
    for row_idx in range(table.num_rows):
        # ---- timestamp or sequence number ----
        ts_scalar = frame_col[row_idx]
        frame_ts = ts_scalar.value
        # ---- zero-copy bytes ----
        inner = buf_col[row_idx][0]
        pixels = inner.values.to_numpy(zero_copy_only=False)
        # ---- width/height ----
        fmt = fmt_col[row_idx][0]
        w = int(fmt["width"])
        h = int(fmt["height"])
        # ---- reshape -> BGRA8 ----
        img_np = pixels.reshape(h, w, 4)
        # yield
        yield frame_ts, rr.Image(img_np)
```

As you can see, we must query each pyarrow column with hand-crafted deserializer instead of relying on the type automatically having decorators/macros under the hood to handle. Although this is a consequence of an OLAP / columnar storage format, that does not mean users must suffer !

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Akin to a typical ECS, we should be able to iter the table given a type

```
def iter_color_frames(rrd_path: str):
  rrd = rr.dataframe.load_recording(rrd_path)
  view = rrd.view(index=timeline, contents="...path")
  for row in view.select(rr.Image):
     ....
```
**Describe alternatives you've considered**
there's lots of ways to slice this problem ... but it can be measured by # lines of code for devs

**Additional context**
Mirror game engines with ECS semantics - like Bevy

data.title: [Feature Request] TensorView: Support for overlaying Segmentation Masks on 3D Tensors
data.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
I am using Rerun to visualize medical imaging data (MRI in .nii.gz format). I log the raw MRI volume as a `Tensor` and visualize it using `TensorView` to scroll through slices.

However, I also have a brain segmentation mask (also a 3D volume) that I need to validate against the MRI. Currently, `TensorView` only seems to support visualizing a single tensor at a time. I cannot overlay the segmentation mask on top of the MRI slices as I would in 2D using `SegmentationImage`.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I would like `TensorView` (or a similar volume slicing view) to support:
1.  **Multi-tensor layering:** The ability to select multiple tensor entities in the Blueprint.
2.  **Segmentation Overlay:** Specifically, the ability to overlay an integer-based tensor (mask) on a float-based tensor (image), utilizing `AnnotationContext` for coloring and opacity.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
-   Converting the 3D segmentation to a `Mesh3D` using marching cubes. This works for the 3D spatial view but does not allow for precise slice-by-slice validation of the segmentation boundaries against the pixel data.
-   Manually "burning" the segmentation into the MRI pixel data before logging (this destroys the original data values).

**Additional context**
This is a standard feature in medical imaging viewers (like ITK-SNAP or 3D Slicer) and is critical for debugging 3D segmentation models.

data.title: Cannot send 2GiB+ chunks over gRPC
Support "frame locked" `CoordinateFrames`
data.body:
[ROS' Marker type](https://docs.ros.org/en/noetic/api/visualization_msgs/html/msg/Marker.html) has a `frame_locked` property documented as `# If this marker should be frame-locked, i.e. retransformed into its frame every timestep`
(Also shows up in Foxglove: https://docs.foxglove.dev/docs/sdk/schemas/scene-entity)

The `CoordinateFrame` archetype should have this as well to make data migration easier.

Right now its not entirely straight forward to work around this: in order to lock to an old frame the easiest thign to do is to create a new frame with a relationship to the target frame that has the desired relation.

Looking at our current implementation for ros style transforms (and tree handling in general) this feature seems rather tricky at first: we currently only ever compute the latest-at transform tree for the current frame, making it hard to go backwards in time for a given frame relationship.
However, the problems in regard to caching paths/transforms are somewhat similar to transform interpolation, so I'd suggest that we keep this in mind when improving our abilities there.

data.title: Fix clear <-> static interaction for Transforms3D
data.body:
From https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/pull/11909:

We talked about this a bit on Slack DM. So turns out my implementation and me are wrong here: one can't clear static data. Example:

```py
import rerun as rr

rr.init("rerun_example_points3d", spawn=True)
rr.set_time("timetime", duration=1.0)
rr.log("points", rr.Points3D([[0, 0, 0], [1, 1, 1]]), static=True)
rr.log("points", rr.LineStrips3D([[0, 0, 0], [1, 1, 1]]), static=False)
rr.set_time("timetime", duration=2.0)
rr.log("points", rr.Clear(recursive=False))
```

This will still show the points after t=2 but not the line.
Fixing this will require us to store a "static flag" every atomic set (transforms, instance poses, pinholes) which then makes us disregard all new temporal data

I'll fix this & test this in a separate iteration.

_Originally posted by @Wumpf in https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/11909#issuecomment-3547701011_

data.title: Cache chunk time statistics for efficient data density sampling
data.body:
Implementing #10102 in #11766 resulted in a performance regression.
This happens because computing the required `Chunk::num_events_cumulative_per_unique_time_unsorted` takes a lot of time.

We should be able to cache this value and avoid recomputing it each frame, this would make it easier to even more fine grained sampling from chunks and create a better data density graph.

data.title: Partial blueprint updates

labels.name: 🟦 blueprint
labels.description: The data that defines our UI

data.body:
Brought up by @danielduberg 

After logging a full blueprint, we want to update the camera pose many times, in order to animate the camera.
What's missing is a way to log partial blueprints. Example API:


```py
view_3d = rrb.Spatial3DView(name="3D", origin="world");
blueprint = rrb.Horizontal(
    view_3d,
    rrb.Spatial2DView(name="2D", origin="other"),
  )
rr.send_blueprint(blueprint)

log_some_data()

# Animate the camera
for i in range(0, 100):
    eye_controls=rrb.EyeControls3D(
          position=(i, 0.0, 2.0),
          look_target=(0.0, 2.0, 0.0),
          eye_up=(-1.0, 0.0, 0.0),
          kind=rrb.Eye3DKind.FirstPerson,
          speed=20.0,
      )
      rr.log_blueprint(f"{view_3d.blueprint_path()/EyeControls3D", eye_controls)   # <- this is what's missing
      sleep(0.1)
```

We already have `view.blueprint_path()`; what lacking is an ergonomic way (or any way at all?) to log to the _blueprint_ store rather than to the recording store.

A nicer API would be to get a blueprint stream from a data stream, or similar:

```py
stream.log("data", …)
stream.blueprint().log("blueprint", …)
```

data.title: Handle SIGINT in the python catalog SDK
data.body:
The python interpreter handles SIGINT regularly between instruction. However, it doesn't do it _durring_ FFI calls. So when we `wait_for_future` for a long time (e.g because the server is slow or stalling), ctrl-C doesn't interrupt the waiting.


It would appear that the solution to that is to use `[PyErr_CheckSignals](https://docs.python.org/3/c-api/exceptions.html#c.PyErr_CheckSignals)`. We could poll it in parallel to `f` in the implementation of `wait_for_future`, and early out with an `Interrupted` error. Maybe?

Background:
- https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62364030/keyboard-interrupt-from-python-does-not-abort-rust-function-pyo3/62380114#62380114

Ideally the parsing for these two would be done separately, and getting to remove all of the `serde(skip)` and unnecessary serde derives on `TimePanel` and `SelectionPanel`.

data.title: Webviewer does not show large chunks when memory limit is exceeded but blocks memory
data.body:
**Describe the bug**
While investigating another issue [11699](<https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/11699>) about beeing unable to increase the memory limit I noticed that pushing larger chunks of data using rr.send_columns can result in having memory allocated (according to memory panel) but not showing up. At the same time i get the message that data has been dropped. The funny thing is, that the stack of images I'm pushing here is about 1 GB when I get the "drop message" even though it says I have a memory limit of 2.3 GB.

**To Reproduce**
Start grpc and webviewer using e.g. `rerun --serve-web` and push a large chunk of data in it, using `rr.send_columns` that causes data to be dropped.

Or use this script:
(be aware that it might also crash the viewer ...)

```
# %%
import rerun as rr
import numpy as np

rr.init(application_id="rerun_example_serve_web_viewer", spawn=False)
# Start a gRPC server and use it as log sink.
server_uri = rr.serve_grpc(server_memory_limit="500MB")

# Connect the web viewer to the gRPC server and open it in the browser
rr.serve_web_viewer(connect_to=server_uri, open_browser=True)
img = np.random.randint(0,255,(10000,50000))
print(f"Image Size: {img.nbytes*1E-6} MB")
rr.log('test_img', entity=rr.Image(img))

# now log an image chunk:
#%%
def log_image_batch(
    entity_path: str,
    times: np.ndarray,
    image_batch: np.ndarray,
    transform: rr.Transform3D = None,
    recording: rr.RecordingStream = None,  # optional if we want to send the data to recording which is not the currently activated one
):
    """
    Log a batch of images to the specified entity path all at once.

    Parameters
    ----------
    entity_path : str
        The path where the images will be logged.
    times : np.ndarray
        An array of timestamps corresponding to each image in the batch.
    image_batch : np.ndarray
        A batch of images to be logged. The shape should be (N, H, W, C) for color images or (N, H, W) for grayscale images.
    transform : rr.Transform3D, optional
        A transformation to be applied to the images. Default is None.
    recording : rr.RecordingStream, optional
        The recording stream to which the data will be sent. Default is None.

    Returns
    -------
    None
    """

    # Log the ImageFormat and indicator once, as static.
    color_model = "RGB" if len(image_batch.shape) > 3 else "L"
    channel_datatype = "U8" if image_batch.dtype == np.uint8 else "U16"
    format_static = rr.components.ImageFormat(
        width=image_batch.shape[2],
        height=image_batch.shape[1],
        color_model=color_model,
        channel_datatype=channel_datatype,
    )

    batch = rr.components.ImageBufferBatch(
        np.frombuffer(image_batch.tobytes(), dtype=np.uint8).reshape(
            [
                image_batch.shape[0],
                image_batch[0].nbytes,
            ]
        ),
    )

    rr.log(
        entity_path,
        rr.Image.from_fields(format=format_static),
        static=True,
        recording=recording,
    )

    if transform is not None:
        rr.log(
            entity_path=entity_path,
            entity=transform,
            static=True,
            recording=recording,
        )

    # Reshape the images so `ImageBufferBatch` can tell that this is several blobs.

    rr.send_columns(
        entity_path,
        indexes=[rr.TimeColumn("time", duration=times)],
        columns=rr.Image.columns(buffer=batch),
        recording=recording if recording is not None else None,
    )

n = 2000
imgs = np.random.randint(0, 255, (n, 480, 640, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
print(f"Image batch size: {imgs.nbytes / 1e6} MB")
times = np.arange(n) * 0.1

log_image_batch("test_batch", times=times, image_batch=imgs)
```

**Expected behavior**
Best result would be at least showing me all data that has been pushed, OR clear all the memory that it would have consumed.

Windows 11 Enterprise Version10.0.22631 Build 22631
System Model: HP ZBook Fury 16 G10 Mobile Workstation PC
Processor: 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13850HX, 2100 Mhz, 20 Core(s), 28 Logical Processor(s)
Installed Physical Memory (RAM): 32,0 GB

data.title: Get rid of `docs-latest`
data.body:
Our current release process _force pushes_ to the `docs-latest` branch, which triggers a separate workflow that builds the search index, and publishes a new version of our docs (https://rerun.io/docs).

We want to be able to make changes to the docs through PRs in this repository, so we also support automatically cherry-picking changes from PRs to the `docs-latest` branch.

When creating patch releases, we branch off of the previous patch release tag. This can cause regressions in our docs if these cherry-picked commits are not cherry-picked onto that new patch release branch. The commits won't be lost, as they are always pushed to `main` first, but it is annoying to have to fix that manually.

We would like to make dealing with `docs-latest` completely automatic and fool-proof. It serves as the website's pointer to "latest documentation content", and we need that to work. This approach has created a good amount of confusion for our team.

## Versioned docs

Here's a potential solution: Get rid of `docs-latest`, and version our docs instead.

Our docs are built from the archive of this repository. But that doesn't need to come from GitHub at all! We can treat our entire repository (or just the `/docs` subset of it) as another build artifact, and upload it to GCS. The website can then load this artifact, and build the site from it.

Not only that, we can maintain an index of all previous releases, allowing us to finally version our main docs site. We can combine this with our ability to point dynamically change the version of the Viewer used on our website to ensure that snippets and the like are not opened in a newer version of the viewer.

One downside is that with how our website is currently architected, every new version will slightly increase build times of https://rerun.io. There are various possible mitigations for that, like using incremental static regeneration to render a given version of our docs the first time it's visited, and then cache it until we need to redeploy the site.

data.title: Verify that `VideoStream` playback works with newest-first gRPC proxy mode

labels.name: feat-video
labels.description: anything video decoding, player, querying, data modelling of videos etc.

data.body:
We have a gRPC proxy mode where we send chunks to the viewer in reverse order (newest first).

Does this work with `VideoStream`?

Note that there are two types of issues to worry about:
* Individual chunks being "unordered" (not all timelines increasing monotonically with RowId)
* Chunks arriving out-of-order

I _believe_ the only problem we have with `VideoStream` is related to the FIRST of these issues, and that the `--newest-first` mode doesn't affect it at all - but let's verify.

data.title: Improve documentation for micro batcher defaults
data.body: **Description:** When I log only Markdown text using `rr.TextDocument` with `MediaType.MARKDOWN`, the text updates appear in real time in the Rerun Viewer. However, if I also log images (`rr.Image`) in the same loop, the Markdown text only appears after a long delay. It looks like the viewer buffers too much data before rendering the text when images are present. This makes it difficult to see status updates in real time. **Code snippet:** ```python while self.running: try: rr.log( "sys.info", rr.TextDocument( f''' # System Information vision/llm_text: {self.llm_text} arm/status: {self.arm_status} '''.strip(), media_type=rr.MediaType.MARKDOWN, ), static=not LOG_WITH_TIMESTAMP ) if not self.camera_image.empty(): img = self.camera_image.get_nowait() rr.log("vision/camera_image", rr.Image(img, color_model=rr.ColorModel.BGR), static=not LOG_WITH_TIMESTAMP) if self.object_coordinates and len(self.object_coordinates) == 4: x1, y1, x2, y2 = self.object_coordinates h, w = img.shape[:2] x1 = max(0, min(x1, w-1)) y1 = max(0, min(y1, h-1)) x2 = max(0, min(x2, w-1)) y2 = max(0, min(y2, h-1)) rr.log("vision/camera_image", rr.Boxes2D(array=[x1, y1, x2, y2], array_format=rr.Box2DFormat.XYXY, labels=self.object_name, colors=[0, 255, 0]), static=not LOG_WITH_TIMESTAMP) if not self.state_machine_graph.empty(): img = self.state_machine_graph.get_nowait() rr.log("state_machine/graph", rr.Image(img, color_model=rr.ColorModel.BGR), static=not LOG_WITH_TIMESTAMP) ``` **Reproduce:** 1. Log only `rr.TextDocument` → text appears in real time. 2. Log both `rr.TextDocument` and `rr.Image` → text display is delayed significantly. **Screenshots:** 1. **Only logging Markdown text** The `sys.info` panel updates immediately with new text. 2. **Logging images and Markdown together** Camera image and state machine graph show up correctly, but the Markdown panel (`sys.info`) stays empty for a long time. 3. **Delayed Markdown update** After some time, a batch of Markdown text suddenly appears. In the timeline view (circled in red), you can see that text logs are recorded discontinuously. This burst-pause-burst pattern repeats over time when images are logged together with text.

data.title: Refactor `ConnectionClient` to avoid the unnecessary endpoint call for token validation
Untangle wheel build for better artifact re-use (and improved CI performance)
data.body:
Better job sequencing for wheel builds could improve things a lot! Build the wasm, cli, and wheels in parallel, adding in any necessary hacks to make them ignore the absence of something they depend on:

* cli is built without the wasm blob by allocating empty space for it in the binary
* patch the binary later to include the wasm once it's available
* wheels don't depend on CLI for the build at all. a wheel is just a zip file, so we can add the CLI to the right place in the archive later

there's also the notebook wheel, which requires that the wasm is available at the time of wheel packing. it's not necessary for the build, that's just some javascript bundling stuff which can be done independently. so it can also be built in parallel with the wasm, cli, and sdk wheel. then combined with the wasm just like the sdk wheel with the CLI.
generally speaking, all of these builds individually finish within like 5 minutes, so we could shorten the entire wheel build path down to roughly that with these changes

(via Jan in https://rerunio.slack.com/archives/C08TEFXNHB2/p1756293630686379?thread_ts=1756130152.285669&cid=C08TEFXNHB2)

labels.description: This is a pressing issue for one of our users

labels.name: 🪵 Log & send APIs
labels.description: Affects the user-facing API for all languages

data.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When trying to create `Transform3D` objects with xyz and rpy (roll, pitch, yaw) data, there is no native support for euler angles. This means external libraries need to be used to first convert euler data to quaternion data which Rotation3D can use.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'm still a bit confused about components vs archetypes vs datatypes vs utility types (like [Rotation3D](https://ref.rerun.io/docs/cpp/structrerun_1_1Rotation3D.html)), but it seems like a new component called `RotationEuler` would make the most sense and be consistent with the existing `RotationAxisAngle` and `RotationQuat`.

Or maybe a new datatype called `EulerAngles` would be sufficient, as long as other types like `Rotation3D` could be constructed from `EulerAngles`, so that you can use it across the other API functions like `Transform3D` constructors.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Use third-party libraries to first convert to quaternion (scipy for python, tf2 for C++).

data.body:
I often see a lot of 3rd party crates (like datafusion) recompiling every day. Why?

## Suspect A: feature flags
* Investigated in https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/pull/10933

## ✅ Suspect B: pixi
* Run `cargo build`
* Run `pixi run cargo build` - A LOT of thing recompiles - WHY??
* Run `cargo build` again -  A LOT of thing recompiles _again_

What is different?

These things look the same within and without my environment:

* `cargo --version`
* `rustc --version`
* `env | grep -E "(RUST|CARGO)"`
* `pixi run cargo metadata --format-version 1`

Solution: put pixi-cargo builds into own `target_pixi` folder:
* https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/pull/10935

## Suspect C: 3rd party `build.rs` files
Most (all?) of the crates we keep recompiling have their own `build.rs` files. Likely not a coincidence.
The `pixi` stuff above casued 3rd `build.rs` to invalidate their crates.
Not sure yet if they are still under suspicion after we solve A and B. TBD.

data.title: Leverage DLPack for Generic Performant Tensor Support
data.body:
In [this](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/pull/10647) PR and the [follow on](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/pull/10666) (since dlpack only supports some datatypes) we added minimal support to a range of tensor formats through the [dlpack](https://dmlc.github.io/dlpack/latest/) protocol. As of writing this pytorch and Jax automatically. Tensorflow still seems to be rolling out support.

Right now we add support for torch tensors on a per use case basis with a typing ignore flag: example https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/blob/19441260a53b1ae09c9df859ccd344c1ff1b37d0/rerun_py/rerun_sdk/rerun/archetypes/image_ext.py#L51

I believe that we can check for __dlpack__ and generically support a broader range of inputs while reducing our code duplication. This should also let us avoid the attribute error entirely which according to the code comment is slow.

data.title: MCAP `MessageLayers` should only look at relevant chunks

labels.name: 🧢 MCAP
labels.description: Everything related to the MCAP support

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

data.body:
Currently, we still iterate over an entire MCAP file to retrieve all the messages that are relevant for a given `dyn MessageLayer`. We should abstract of the `::mcap::Summary` and `mcap_bytes` to allow indexed access + filtering of the MCAP file.

We should be able to:

* Filter by topic
* Filter by time range

Each `MessageLayer` should specify the `encoding` or `schema` of messages that it is interested in and then get presented only those messages. This is required large MCAP files, as well as presenting more useful errors on a per-layer basis.

data.title: Support timeline control and range selection events in the native viewer

labels.name: 🟦 blueprint
labels.description: The data that defines our UI

labels.name: 🪵 Log & send APIs
labels.description: Affects the user-facing API for all languages

data.body:
<!--
First look if there is already a similar feature request. If there is, upvote the issue with 👍
-->

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
#8673 added support for selecting timelines and timepoints in the web viewer through the JS API. However, it does not currently appear possible to do the same for the native viewer through Rust.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
It would be useful to have API-level control of the timeline at least through Rust, if not the other SDK languages. Ideally, this would include support for registering callbacks for timeline events **including** range selection (e.g., shift+drag selection), extending the existing support for time update events and timeline selection events.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Duplicating the timeline somehow in an extended GUI - but then it's unclear if I could sync the state with the "real" timeline in a native viewer...

**Additional context**
This is intended for use in building a data annotation app extending the Rerun GUI, wherein I need to be able to select sub-ranges of a recording and send these time bounds to my extension app for further processing.

See also https://discord.com/channels/1062300748202921994/1402749709868859433 and https://discord.com/channels/1062300748202921994/1075873257124810852/1402748262842110213

data.title: Allow for merging recordings within the viewer
data.body:
**Problem statement**

Sometimes data is spread between multiple recordings. These can be recordings at the same time and same event but to different places on disk (say if it's distributed, or if a recording was created from a post-process routine like in creation of image embeddings). These could also be the same event that got split between files (for efficiency or because of interruption). Combining these recordings into one brings all the data together, making it play better with visualization and data set creation.

The problems, more generally:

* data was recorded in different places
* data recording was interrupted
* data files are cycled for efficiency reasons
* post-processed data needs to be added to the original recording (embeddings, e.g.)
* compare two runs side-by-side

**Goal / value**

Ship an in-viewer affordance that lets a user pick 2+ files and create a (virtual?) merged partition.

**Scope**

There are two potential modes:

1. Concatenate — keep original timestamps, simply interleave/append records.
2. Align — resample all recordings to the same timeline. Helpful especially in comparing episodes side-by-side.

For this ticket, let's first validate with `concat` mode. Align could be a more advanced use case, so needs some better validation.

Merging, also, should not overwrite the existing recordings but create a new one. If technically feasible, this new one could be *virtual* in that data is not actually copied, just references/pointers to the data are created.

**User Journey**

An example user journey for this feature *could* look like:

* In my partition table, I multi-select (shift + click, ctrl + click, or checkboxes) the partitions I want to merge
* Right-click on a selected item and "Merge partitions…" becomes active
* A dialogue appears asking me to name the new partition.
  * Eventually, it'll also ask if we want to reindex to a particular partition. Needs source partition and timeline.
* My screen scrolls to and selects the newly created partition.
* I click "Open" and see that it's been merged
* speculative: If virtual, I want to save this, so choose "export to RRD" from some place

**Open questions**

1. Should merged views persist in the workspace history or be transient?

**See also**

`rosbag merge` [🔗](https://pypi.org/project/rosbag-merge/)

`mcap merge` [🔗](https://pypi.org/project/rosbag-merge/)

data.title: Introduce a `Flag` component for grouping/filtering
data.body:
## Desired functionality
A reoccurring feature request is to be able to quickly filter what's shown in the viewer:

* Show only things from "Robot A"
* Show only cameras
* Hide everything related to motion planning
* …

This is particularly useful when you have a very "busy" 3D view.

## `Flag` component solution
I suggest we add a new string component called `Flag` (*).
* Each entity can have any number of flags
* The flags form a set
  * The order of the flags are not important
  * Repeated flags doesn't matter
* We encourage `PascalCase` for the flags?
  * Encouraging/enforcing a specific (space-less) casing would enable using the flag names without quotes in some future DSL
  * Helps prevents stupid mistakes like writing `car wheel` in one place and `CarWheel` in another

### The UI
In the UI we can then have a filter functionality to
* Hide everything with a specific flag ("mute")
* Show only things with a specific flag ("solo")
* Combinations of the above

The UI could either be per-view, or global (unclear what is best here 🤔).

### How does flags interact with the entity hierarchy?
If `/skoda` has a `Car` flag, will `/skoda/wheels` be shown when `Car` is on solo?

### (*) The `Flag` name
A more natural name choice would be `Tag`, but that would be confusing, because of what we call "tagged components", which is something completely different.

Alternative names:
* `Tag`
* `Flag` 
* `Label` - already used for 
* `Group` - slightly obscures the fact that each entity can belong to multiple groups
* `Marker` - conflicts with plot markers
* `Badge`
* …

## Similar feature
We already have `ClassId`, which is an integer, used for segmentation images.

data.title: Support attaching custom data to each pixel in an image

labels.name: user-request
labels.description: This is a pressing issue for one of our users

data.body:
Suppose you have an RGB image, and for each pixel you want to attach some custom data, such as:

* label: string
* confidence: f32
* …

How would you do it? I see three different ways of doing it:

## A) Log a box per pixel
Log an extra `Boxes2D` entity, instanced so that you end up with one box per pixel. You can then attach custom components to that entity.

This is the ugliest solution, but also the only one that works reliably at the moment.

**Pros:**
* Works today
* Supports any and all component types (you can even attach an image to each pixel of an image, e.g. for light-field visualization)

**Cons:**
* https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/10276
* A lot of tiny boxes cover your image
* Hacky
* Requires a separate child entity

## B) Log an extra image per custom data
Log multiple images to sibling entities, one for each type of custom data.

For instance, you could log `confidence` as a `Luminance` image with datatype `f32`.

**Pros:**
* Works today
* Pro: you can visualize the confidence image with color mapping

**Cons:**
* `Image` is limited in the types it supports (each pixel can only be L, RGB, or RGBA, of u8, u16, f32 etc)
  * No support for strings (but can often be done with `SegmentationImage`)
  * No support for e.g. a jacobian per pixel
  * No support for custom components
  * Has wrong semantic meaning (encoding "confidence" as "luminance" doesn't really make sense)
* Our support for stacking dozens of images on top of each other is poor (but can be fixed)
  * We don't show all of them when hovering
  * What image ends up on top is not well-defined
  * It's difficult to configure which image ends up on top
  * It's difficult to configure the transparency of each image
* `Image`s are not really made to be vessels of custom data
  * we could use a `Tensor` instead, but it's not a lot better

## C) Add support for "projecting" components onto pixels
The user would log a single 640x480 RGB image, together with 307200 values for a custom "confidence" component, and a 307200 strings with labels, etc. They would log these components to the same entity.

If the user hovers the pixel at (X=52, Y=23) we translate that to pixel number 52+23*640=14772, and then look up the values of the 14772:th instance of all components at this entity path, and show that in the tooltip when hovering an image.

**Pros:**
* Supports all custom components
* Easy to implement

**Cons:**
* Slightly hacky
  * The selection panel would show a single image and 307200 floats, for instance
  * What happens if the number of components is different from WxH?
* This would be slightly nicer if we supported nullable components, which we want to remove:
  * https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/6819
  * …but empty strings, and `NaN`, etc is often good-enough

**Related:**
* #1756

data.title: Static Table Tries to Return Scroll Bar Every Timestamp
data.body:
**Describe the bug**
The WIP mcap conversion creates a table to denote which schemas we weren't able to infer. If there are a lot of those then there is a scroll bar. As the timeline plays the scroll bar fights to return to its starting point. This isn't mcap specific but that's where I discovered it.

data.title: Send intermediate results/chunks for datafusion table providers
data.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

This is a follow on to https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/pull/10698 

In that PR we send a fully partition's worth of data at a time. Instead we should be able to stream out intermediate results once we have enough chunks to do so.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

From our first gRPC call, we know the chunk IDs and their associated time. We should be able to determine when we have received all prior rows for a given time of interest. Once all of those chunks have been received, stream out a row. This will give intermediate results instead of waiting for the entire partition to be received.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Leave as is, which is still better than collecting everything in memory

**Additional context**

- It's unclear to me how we can verify the timing of when the chunks arrived
- There is an opportunity to exit early when we've reached our row limit.

data.title: Dataframe should be able to query the same component logged to the same timestamp multiple times

labels.name: feat-dataframe-api
labels.description: Everything related to the dataframe API

data.body:
**Describe the bug**
If I send a column twice both get stored in the `rrd` but on a dataframe query we can only grab the latest.

**To Reproduce**
Running this will write the same column but slightly different twice in a row. If we only call `write_n` then the file size is half as large.
```python
def create_sample() -> str:
    batch_size = 1024
    embedding_dim = 768
    rrd_name = "<path>.rrd"

    stream = rr.RecordingStream(application_id="sample_name", recording_id="uuid", send_properties=True)
    stream.save(rrd_name)
    data = np.zeros((batch_size, embedding_dim), dtype=np.uint8)

    def write_n(n: int, offset: int = 0) -> None:
        for i in range(n):
            time_column = rr.TimeColumn("log_tick", sequence=np.arange(i * batch_size, (i + 1) * batch_size))
            stream.send_columns(
                entity_path="/camera/ext1",
                indexes=[time_column],
                columns=rr.AnyValues.columns(embeddings=(data + offset).flatten()).partition(
                    [embedding_dim] * batch_size
                ),
            )
        stream.flush(True)

    write_n(5)
    write_n(5, offset=1)
    return rrd_name
```

Then if we try to query out the result we only get one set of values
```python
rrd_name = create_sample()
rec = rr.dataframe.load_recording(rrd_name)
view = rec.view(index="log_tick", contents={"/camera/ext1": "embeddings"})
rb = view.select()
total_rows = 0
print(rec.schema())
for batch in rb:
    total_rows += batch.num_rows
print(total_rows)
```

**Expected behavior**
Either a warning/error on overwriting or if we are filtering unique values then the file size on disk to be the same as calling write once. Or maybe some mechanism to access the overwritten values.

**Rerun version**
rerun-cli 0.24.0 (default map_view nasm native_viewer release web_viewer) [rustc 1.85.0 (4d91de4e4 2025-02-17), LLVM 19.1.7] aarch64-apple-darwin release-0.24.0 cf9dc2b, built 2025-07-17T14:42:07Z
Video features: av1 default ffmpeg nasm serde

data.title: Simplify Row Count Inspection Viewer and SDK
data.body: ## Motivation I wanted to confirm that I had processed data correctly so the first check was to see how many rows were in the column of interest. In the viewer hovering over the streams window show how many times things were LOGGED to that. Meanwhile in the sdk we can load an rrd and count rows like such. ```python >>rec = rr.dataframe.load_recording(rrd_name) >>view = rec.view(index="log_tick", contents={"/camera/ext1": "embeddings"}) >>rb = view.select() >>total_rows = 0 >>for batch in rb: ...total_rows += batch.num_rows >>print(total_rows) 5120 ``` These two values can be different if someone has a typo where they log duplicates: ```python def create_sample() -> str: batch_size = 1024 embedding_dim = 768 rrd_name = "" stream = rr.RecordingStream(application_id="sample_name", recording_id="uuid", send_properties=True) stream.save(rrd_name) data = np.zeros((batch_size, embedding_dim), dtype=np.uint8) def write_n(n: int) -> None: for i in range(n): time_column = rr.TimeColumn("log_tick", sequence=np.arange(i * batch_size, (i + 1) * batch_size)) stream.send_columns( entity_path="/camera/ext1", indexes=[time_column], columns=rr.AnyValues.columns(embeddings=data.flatten()).partition([embedding_dim] * batch_size), ) stream.flush(True) write_n(5) write_n(5) return rrd_name ``` ## Suggestions It would be nice to get the actual row count in an easier fashion for a given column. In the viewer when we select an entity we get a nice side window that I believe comes from our schema. If our schema provided a row count that might make a simpler way to get the answer on the sdk and provide it through the gui as well.

data.title: Update the JS/notebook APIs to use `StoreId` instead of recording id
data.body:
- follow-up to: https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/pull/10742

`StoreId`, which uniquely identify logical recordings are displayed by the viewer, now contains both the application id and the recording id. However, the whole `WebHandle` JS api refers to recording by `recording_id: &str` only. This is both fragile and inconsistent, and needs to be updated.

This needs some design work though. A naive update could be to add `application_id: &str` arguments everywhere, or introduce a `RecordingStoreId { application_id: String, recording_id : String }` construct.

However:
- In the remote dataset context, we've now turned to using URI to refer to recording, including in notebook context when interacting with the viewer.
- As we want to narrow down the scope of our specifier ("focus on this view and this time range of this recording, using this blueprint") URIs scale better than hard-coded APIs.

In view of that, it would appear to make sense to more generally migrate to a URI-based approach to referring to recordings. (This is also related to the goal of better exposing the viewer's memory store as a server.)

data.title: Steps to remove `StoreId`-related 0.24 backward compatibility

labels.name: 🚜 refactor
labels.description: Change the code, not the functionality

data.body:
Between 0.24 and 0.25, `StoreId` was changed to include the application id (see [https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/10509](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/10509)). At the grpc level, this meant that:

* `StoreInfo` should no longer have an `application_id` (it moved to the `StoreId` it contains)
* legacy `ArrowMessage` and `BlueprintActivationMessage` are tricky to migrate because they only contain a `StoreId`, which used to not have an application id.

As a result, we introduced a number of mechanisms for migration, including:

* backward compatible grpc schema update
* "smart" grpc message to native object migration
* a cache system in the decoding streams

If/when we decided to drop 0.24 rrd compatibility (which could happen at the earliest for the 0.26 release), we should cleanup the code from all these mechanisms. Look for TODOs marked with this issue number.

**IMPORTANT**: the `rerun rrd` CLI tools, including `migrate`, `route`, `compare`, and possible others, use the `Decoder` facility. As a result, reverting the migration code in `Decoder` would _also_ remove the capacity of these CLI tools to handle legacy, pre-0.25 rrd. We must decide if this is a problem or not. If it is and we still want to clean-up the code base, we might have to port the migration logic to some CLI specific utility (e.g. maybe a grpc-level prefilter).

data.title: Mitigate depth precision issues

labels.name: 😤 annoying
labels.description: Something in the UI / SDK is annoying to use

data.body:
Occasionally we get reports of flickering points and lines caused by too large coordinates. This happens due to precision issues in the shaders, i.e. transformation/projection math as well as the "ray tracing" we do in point & line shaders (which is why it always shows up first there)

We're already using inverse infinite f32 depth buffer which is known to be the [best option for depth buffers](https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/visualizing-depth-precision/), so there's not much we can do from this side. However there's a few things we should look into:

* [ ] configurable near plane
    * our camera near plane is hardcoded right now!
    * moving the camera near plane has enormous consequence of precision for anything far away
* [ ] adaptive near plane?
    * see above, but could we make this automatic to some extent? As you move further away from the origin, use a higher near plane by default using some heuristic founded in precision estimates?
* [ ] revisit points & line alpha discard math
    * surely we do a lot of things there that could be done in a more numerical stable way?
* [ ] consider limit camera zoom/position. If precision gets too poor (at some point even our world grid flickers), maybe we shouldn't allow these positions or warn?



Issues & conversations where this issues came up (incomplete list):
* https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/2754

data.title: Allow marking decoder re-entrant points (keyframes) on `VideoStream`

labels.name: feat-video
labels.description: anything video decoding, player, querying, data modelling of videos etc.

data.body:
`VideoStream` is design to map directly to simple ROS messages and will automatically determine if a frame is decoder re-entrant.
However, for any query into video data, it would be useful to know when one has queried enough data for display/decoding.

"Decoder re-entrant" is a fancy way of saying that a decoder can start at that sample and when continuously fed samples (in correct decoder order) will operate correctly. I.e. all seeks have to snap to these re-entrant frames.
Re-entrancy _usally_ means that the frame is an I-frame, which _usually_ means that this is the start of a group of pictures. Caution is advised with those terms since they are very decoder dependent and one gets quickly lost in details, both technical and naming. E.g. many codecs distinguishe open and closed group of pictures, H264/H265 distininguish IDR (instant decoder refresh) frames from regular I frames, etc.
Exact vocabulary in this space is difficult!

Practically we should store this as an optional boolean per video sample. Since we already implement the oracle to determine it from frame, we can handle this in the viewer like a fallback provider.

Naming discussion for such a property:
* `is_sync` - this is what we use internally and is derived from MP4's [Sync Sample Atom](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/quicktime-file-format/sync_sample_atom)
   * also talks about keyframes though on that doc page!
* `is_keyframe` - a lot more accessible!
   * Is it accurate?
      * [AV1 specs](https://aomediacodec.github.io/av1-spec/av1-spec.pdf) "key frame" as decoder reentrant: "An Intra frame which resets the decoding process when it is shown."
      * H264 & H265: We can clarify that this is an IDR in H264 & H265
      * VP9 has super-frames as an organizational unit but is otherwise delightfully simple: "There are only two frame types in VP9. Intra frames or key frames are decoded without reference to any other frame in a sequence" ([source](http://downloads.webmproject.org/docs/vp9/vp9-bitstream_superframe-and-uncompressed-header_v1.0.pdf))
    * begs the question whether we should also allow tagging b-frames and p-frames, i.e. `frame_type`. Maybe we should make this an enum to keep this possibility open? Care is advised though because of above mentioned nomenclature jungle and it's questionable whether the distinction of p-frame and b-frame is all that valuable for the usecases we want to support

data.title: Towards an ergonomic Rust client wrapper over redap grpc frontend

labels.name: 🚜 refactor
labels.description: Change the code, not the functionality

data.body:
### Goal

Short term goal: a one-stop shop, high-level client struct and crate, used everywhere in the viewer and SDK to connect to redap servers.

Long term goal: clean it enough to make it a "public" crate (used by users to interface to redap servers from Rust).

### Status quo

The recently introduced `re_grpc_client::ConnectionClient` aims to do that, although it currently implements only very few endpoints.

Before, the `ConnectionHandle` construct from the Python SDK served the same purpose, albeit in a form that is not suitable outside of the SDK (the short-term intent is to migrate its guts to `ConnectionClient`).

In addition to these "client"-type structures, we have a growing collection of so-called `ext::`version of the protoc-codegen'd grpc messages.They live in `re_protos` and are used by `ConnectionClient` and `ConnectionHandle` whenever possible.

### Problems

* `ConnectionHandle` has way too much logic that should be migrated to `ConnectionClient` (on-going effort).
* `ConnectionClient` is currently in `re_grpc_client`, which contains tools and glue code that are rather viewer-specific (ie. shouldn't be part of a public wrapper).
* Because the `ext::` types live in `re_protos` and due to some circular dependency problem, it's impossible for `ext::` type to implement some kind of helper method. Specifically, types which include a `DataframePart` cannot decode it because they'd need `re_log_encoding`, which depends on `re_protos`.
* The `ConnectionClient` and the types it uses (the `ext::` types) live in different crates, which is somewhat awkward for an API.

### Suggested plan

* Move `ConnectionClient` to its own `re_redap_client` crate (and rename it accordingly). This should be easy as it currently only rely some error type that could be duplicated.
* Move all `ext::` types to `re_redap_client`.
  * Note: the redap server implementation *also* makes extensive use of these `ext::` types. Puling them from a "client" crate would be slightly odd naming-wise, but it should not cause any actual issue.
* Eventually move `ConnectionRegistry`to `re_redap_client` as well (`ConnectionRegistry` keeps tracks of auth credentials and opened connection, and is useful to both the viewer and the SDK—and possibly external users).
  * Need to make `ConnectionRegistery` generic over the `impl GrpcService` type.

### Related

* [https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/pull/10183](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/pull/10183)
* [https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/10188](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/10188)
* [https://github.com/rerun-io/dataplatform/issues/711](https://github.com/rerun-io/dataplatform/issues/711)

type.name: Feature

data.title: Inconsistent definition of a Sorbet batch
data.body:
### Problem

Discussion: https://rerunio.slack.com/archives/C07T0LFT5BQ/p1751033385400169

*(with quite some help from Claude)*

The Rerun viewer currently requires `sorbet:version` metadata for all record batches, but this conflicts with its stated goal of handling arbitrary record batches. The DataFusion widget implementation assumes every record batch to  SorbetBatch compatibility, creating errors when processing general record batches lacking Sorbet metadata.

This became apparent via:

* #10417 and the corresponding "fix":
* #10418

We should get rid of the inconsistencies and decide what exactly constitutes a SorbetBatch and a ChunkBatch.

**Core Tension:**

* **Intended behavior**: Viewer should accept mixed Sorbet/non-Sorbet data
* **Current implementation**: Strict Sorbet requirements cause migration errors
* **Architectural assumption**: SorbetBatch was designed as lenient "RecordBatch-with-optional-benefits"

**Key Design Questions:**

1. Should `sorbet:version` be batch-level or field-level metadata?
2. How strict should SorbetBatch validation be vs. ChunkBatch?
3. Should migration logic apply to component descriptors in mixed-metadata scenarios?

**Alternative Framings:**

* **Metadata granularity**: Move from batch-level to column-level Sorbet versioning for true mixed-mode support
* **Batch typing**: Establish clear SorbetBatch vs. general RecordBatch handling paths
* **Migration strategy**: Implement best-effort, column-by-column migration rather than batch-level requirements

**Failure Modes:**

* Customer datasets merging different Sorbet versions into single tables
* Performance degradation from redundant validation
* Silent data corruption if migration logic becomes too permissive

**Trade-offs:** Relaxing requirements improves compatibility but may mask legitimate data quality issues. Maintaining strict validation ensures data integrity but limits viewer utility for heterogeneous datasets.

data.title: `GetChunks`: allow filtering by `(entity, component_name` and drop `fuzzy_descriptors`
data.body:
The current implementation of `GetChunksRequest` currently is a poor match for the dataframe query semantics, where you can do e.g:

```python
recording.view(index=...,content={"/entity": ["Positions2D", "Radii"]})
```

This means that there is no way to restrict the downloaded chunks according to the view definition. (The final results *are* correct however, since the dataframe query is run locally on the downloaded chunks and it will honour the view in the final dataframe. So this is primarily an optimisation concern.)

After discussing with @jleibs and @clement, we propose the following course of action:

* we remove `fuzzy_descriptors` from `QueryLatestAt`and `QueryRange`
* we introduce a way to specify a list of `(entity, component_name)` in `GetChunksRequest`
* the same applies for `QueryDataset`

Note: let's stick to the current semantics of `GetChunkRequest`fields being logically AND'd and (nested) `Query` fields being logically OR'd.

data.title: `ComponentColumnDescriptor::is_static` and other metadata flags can be wrong
data.body:
Given a single chunk, it's impossible to know if a column is truly static, or semantically empty. That can only be determined by considering the entire set of chunks comprising a store/recording/partition. Our current implementation of `ComponentColumnDescriptor` does NOT reflect this. As a result, it's `is_static` field (and other metadata flag) can be wrong, depending on how the schema was computed.

- `ChunkBatch::chunk_schema()` -> WRONG (potentially)
- `ChunkStore::schema() -> correct
- `re_chunk_store::SchemaBuilder()` -> correct

This discrepancy should absolutely be captured by our type system by either:
- not having those flag at all when getting a chunk's schema
- having those flag, but clearly identified as "chunk-level" (as opposed to "store-level")

data.title: Support different modes for `re_grpc_server`
data.body:
Following up to [https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/10298](), I believe for most of our users' existing workflows, we don't actually need history at all. It's only useful when you're connecting late and want *all* data (even though for longer recordings you don't get all data either way, since a portion of it will get GC'd!), or you want to simply connect the viewer a bit late. We could support the following modes for the server: 1. No history 2. Store history until the first Viewer connects 3. Full history, with memory limit (1) For e.g. SDK->native Viewer, where we can guarantee the Viewer spawns before the SDK starts sending data).
(2) For web viewers, where we don't know how long it will take for the browser window to open and the web viewer in it to be ready for incoming data. You're still only connecting a single Viewer to the SDK, so there is no need for history.
(3) For use-cases like periodically opening a Viewer to inspect a robot. The history is helpful to see the some amount of data from before you opened the Viewer. Documenting this properly would be super important.

data.title: Sunset dataframe view and replace it with "Convert to table"

labels.name: feat-dataframe-view
labels.description: Everything related to the dataframe view

data.body:
### Background

The dataframe view has always been a bit of an outlier:

* It's (selection panel) UI doesn't fit well with the rest of the views.
* The timeline selection logic is different from the rest of the viewer.
* It can very quickly run into performance problem.

Also, it is more generally problematic because of the strong performance constraints it puts on the dataframe query engine, because the time budget in the context of the viewer is at least 2 orders of magnitude smaller than in other contexts (i.e. it's ok to wait 1s for a query in a notebook, but the dataframe view must render in less than 10ms).

Finally, the fact that the dataframe view is a odd fit introduces a lot of friction with maintenance, which impacts our ability to improve the dataframe query engine.

### Proposal

Realising that the dataframe query engine is a better fit for one-shot queries (as opposed to continuously refreshing views), and noting that the viewer now supports tables, I propose to sunset the dataframe view and replace it with a "convert recording to table" feature:

* It would apply to whatever is the current recording.
* Upon activation, it would display a (modal?) UI exposing all the knobs of the dataframe query engine.
* Once validated, the query would be executed in a background tasks, which, upon completion, would store its result in a new local table entry.
* Stretch goal: the query could be "remembered", and associated with the resulting table, such that it could be manually refreshed by the user.
* Related: the `DatafustionTableWidget` (which is currently used to display table entires) should have the ability to expand rows to display instances (like the current dataframe view is capable of).

An alternative to this proposal would be to maintain simplified version of the dataframe view, trying to balance its current usefulness (and usage, if it actually is substantial?) while reducing the maintenance frictions mentioned above.

### Related

* [https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/10193](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/10193) ([OSS-1334](https://linear.app/rerun/issue/OSS-1334/reconcile-the-legacy-and-dataset-dataframe-query-api))
* [https://github.com/rerun-io/dataplatform/issues/977](https://github.com/rerun-io/dataplatform/issues/977) ([DPF-1786](https://linear.app/rerun/issue/DPF-1786/api-and-contract-updates-for-static-data))

data.title: Allow logging of dictionaries to map semantic names for vectorized logging

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

data.body:
When comparing these two methods:

```python
observation: Dict[str, Any] = robot.get_observation()
for obs, val in observation.items():
    rr.log(f"observation/{obs}", rr.Scalars(val))
```
The benefit is that I can see clearly which line corresponds to which joint:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d88daf0b-ed28-485b-86d0-08985e852ce1)

It would be nice to vectorize this so I don't need to add a loop. However in doing so, I lose the labels:

```python
observation: Dict[str, Any] = robot.get_observation()
rr.log("observation", rr.Scalars(list(observation.values())))
```

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/495e41a5-3df5-4651-9406-055a418bb0c8)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2115f785-58e4-4e0d-a82d-c3c110edae4d)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bed0ee19-28bf-4587-bfdc-72275eabdbca)

It would be nice if I could just log the dict directly:
```python
observation: Dict[str, Any] = robot.get_observation()
rr.log("observation", rr.Scalars(observation))
```
And the index value gets replaced with the dict key in the chart/legend and in the selection pane


I recognize that this may be intentional to only have a list of values, and if you want to name them, then log to new entities. However, one other gain is that we wouldn't need to log the entire list every time. Say in the above code, for whatever reason, the `robot.get_observation()` returns less information (maybe a servo errored out, or it wasn't ready, who knows). Logging in a list style like we did above would create erroneous data, because it expects every index to semantically refer to the same data source. Logging a dict instead would allow for gaps like this.

data.title: Migration from "application" to "dataset"
data.body:
We need to reconcile our old notion of application id with the new notion of dataset.

### Status quo

* "application id" is not an id, but a user-provided string that is not guaranteed to be unique.
  * "Dataset Name" would probably be a better name.
* Datasets have both an id and a name. The former is universally unique, the latter is only unique within a catalog (so *not* unique within the viewer, as it can connect to multiple catalog)
* Application ID are used to index blueprints, ie default/current blueprint is shared across all recording with the same application id.
* Currently, we set the application ID of partitions loaded to the viewer to the dataset ID.

### Workflow challenge

The workflow side of this migration is tricky:

* App id are currently auto-spawned by their mere usage in a recording. The provide "auto-grouping" semantics that are occasionally useful.
* In contrast, dataset are created, and then registered to.

We need to carefully design how the current logging-and-local-debugging workflow should evolve to accommodate the dataset conept.

data.title: Component type registry problem in C++
data.body:
A user reports that they are hitting the following assertion:
```
assertion `left != right` failed: Component type with the same descriptor already registered left: ComponentDescriptor { archetype_name: Some("rerun.archetypes.TextLog"), archetype_field_name: Some("level"), component_name: "rerun.components.TextLogLevel" } right: ComponentDescriptor { archetype_name: Some("rerun.archetypes.TextLog"), archetype_field_name: Some("level"), component_name: "rerun.components.TextLogLevel" }
```

I have not managed to reproduce this myself yet, but along the way I noticed:

data.title: Project: WIP MCAP Dataloader
data.body:
## Background

MCAP is a common format for storing data collected from various sensors and algorithms on the robot. We want native support for this file format, with an easy way to build a partition manifest in the dataplatform.

<details>
<summary>A brief overview of the MCAP file format</summary>
MCAP is a modular container file format for recording timestamped pub/sub messages with arbitrary serialization formats.

An MCAP file follows the following structure:
```
<Magic>
<Header>
<Data section>
[<Summary section>]
[<Summary Offset section>]
<Footer>
<Magic>
```

The header record contains the recording profile which dictates how the data is encoded.

- For ros2 recordings, this profile must be set to `ros2`
    - This profile uses `cdr` encoding, which can be parsed using https://crates.io/crates/cdr

The data section contains records with message data, attachments, and supporting records.

The following records are allowed to appear in the data section:

- [Schema](https://mcap.dev/spec#schema-op0x03)
- [Channel](https://mcap.dev/spec#channel-op0x04)
- [Message](https://mcap.dev/spec#message-op0x05)
- [Attachment](https://mcap.dev/spec#attachment-op0x09)
- [Chunk](https://mcap.dev/spec#chunk-op0x06)
- [Message Index](https://mcap.dev/spec#message-index-op0x07)
- [Metadata](https://mcap.dev/spec#metadata-op0x0c)
- [Data End](https://mcap.dev/spec#data-end-op0x0f)

The last record in the data section MUST be the [Data End](https://mcap.dev/spec#data-end-op0x0f) record.

Example MCAP file layout:

```
[Header]
[Chunk A]
  [Schema A]
  [Channel 1 (A)]
  [Channel 2 (B)]
  [Message on 1]
  [Message on 1]
  [Message on 2]
[Message Index 1]
[Message Index 2]
[Attachment 1]
[Chunk B]
  [Schema B]
  [Channel 3 (B)]
  [Message on 3]
  [Message on 1]
[Message Index 3]
[Message Index 1]
[Data End]
[Schema A]
[Schema B]
[Channel 1]
[Channel 2]
[Channel 3]
[Chunk Index A]
[Chunk Index B]
[Attachment Index 1]
[Statistics]
[Summary Offset 0x01]
[Summary Offset 0x05]
[Summary Offset 0x07]
[Summary Offset 0x08]
[Footer]
```
</details>

This project issue tracks the first version of the MCAP dataloader in Rerun, and what's left before we announce it as "WIP MCAP dataloader, contributions welcome"

## Implementation

### Mapping MCAP chunks to Rerun chunks

In the ROS2 flavor of MCAP, most types can easily be mapped to a Rerun type, however there are some types which do not have a Rerun equivalent which will need some extra massaging.

#### Common ROS2 messages:

- [std_msgs](https://docs.ros.org/en/humble/p/std_msgs/__message_definitions.html)
- [builtin_interfaces](https://docs.ros.org/en/humble/p/builtin_interfaces/__message_definitions.html)
- [sensor_msgs](https://docs.ros.org/en/humble/p/sensor_msgs/__message_definitions.html)
- [geometry_msgs](https://docs.ros.org/en/humble/p/geometry_msgs/__message_definitions.html)


## TODO

- [ ] Initial MCAP Loader
- [ ] Add support for common messages
- [ ] Add example MCAP files to git lfs
- [ ] Add support tests on CI

data.title: Move `Capsules3D` origin to center to align with other primitive shapes

labels.name: 🪵 Log & send APIs
labels.description: Affects the user-facing API for all languages

data.body:
### What

Currently, `Capsules3D` renders with its origin positioned at the bottom of the start cap, which is inconsistent with our other primitive shapes like cubes, ellipsoids, and cylinders (#10139) that all render from their geometric center. 

In an effort to make the api more consistent, we should render capsules with their origin at their geometric center as well.
This is a breaking change in the API so the plan is to:

Remove the `translations` field and add a `centers` field. We then deprecate all existing methods that use the `translations` field and redirect them to use the `centers` field (offsetting the centers by 1/2 the length).

We also need to implement a migration for older data with the `translations` field to the `centers` field. This is a bit tricky because the `translations` field is optional, and might be spread over multiple chunks so it is not trivial to use the length of the capsule. 
This migration benefits from (and almost depends on) #8748, since both the old `translations` and new `centers` fields are optional, it's hard to distinguish between old data that needs migration and fields that are simply absent.

data.title: Manipulate the visibility/properties of a "Group" of Entities

labels.name: 🟦 blueprint
labels.description: The data that defines our UI

data.body:
Apologies if this is a duplicate.

Debugging motion planning workflows are quite unergonomic because there are no convenient ways to show all geometries of a certain "type" (e.g. visual, collision, inertial), or to manipulate the visibility/properties of those geometry types.

---

## Description

Consider the following case where we log visual and collision geometries to every node along the following entity tree:

- `/a/very/deeply/nested/transform/tree`
- `/a/very/deeply/nested/transform/tree/maybe`
- `/a/very/deeply/nested/transform/tree/with`
- `/a/very/deeply/nested/transform/tree/some/branches`

So, for example, the visual geometries might be in:
- `/a/visual/geom_id`
- `/a/very/visual/geom_id`
- `/a/very/deeply/visual/geom_id`
- ...

And the collision geometries:
- `/a/collision/geom_id`
- `/a/very/collision/geom_id`
- `/a/very/deeply/collision/geom_id`
- ...

The Rerun entity tree model is unfortunately not very well suited to isolating the "geometry tree", since the geometries will be distributed amongst the leaves of the entity tree.

---

## The Problem

Now consider how it would be like to "toggle" visibility to see only all the visual geometries vs only all the collision geometries. To do this, we either need to:
1. Generate a blueprint view for each of the geometry types programmatically where the entity filters exhaustively list out the path of each geometry entity (then the user switches which view they are using to see the appropriate geometry type)
2. Exhaustively go through the entire entity tree to toggle the visibility of appropriate geometries one by one

Iirc, for (1) the global matching to be able to toggle something like `/**/collision/*` doesn't work yet, which necessitates exhaustively listing out each geometry entity leaf path.

All of the current options are very unergonomic, and borderline infeasible if done purely in the viewer UI.

## Feature Request

Two options.

### Alternative One

**An alternative to this that I would prefer**, would be to be able to annotate geometry entities with a "group" so that the entire group can be toggled at once. E.g. the visual geometries can be grouped under a "Visual" group and likewise for the collision.

Then there can be a separate UI for toggling properties/visibility of entire groups of entities instead.

Consider how RViz does it

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aad7da7a-10d4-4407-a639-ffc4208e374d)

### Another Alternative

Alternatively, if we could somehow "extract" the geometries into their own tree to more easily manipulate, that could also work.

data.title: Support "Waterfall" style visualizations
data.body:
<!--
First look if there is already a similar feature request. If there is, upvote the issue with 👍
-->

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what the problem is. Ex. I'm always frustrated when […] -->
We have an FPGA monitoring mass spectrometry hardware. The FPGA produces a vector per higher level timestep, per piece of hardware. For example, one of these data streams depicts an RF envelope (1 x 1250 vector of floats).
As these change over time, it's nice to visualize as a 2D tensor.
Currently I'm caching all past vectors and re-logging an ever-growing 2D vector to rerun at each timestep so that data is preserved as expected. This way, scrubbing forward in the viewer "grows" the 2D image downward.
This requires a lot of data duplication and quickly (a couple minutes) becomes unwieldy (gigabytes of memory use).

This is conceptually what a "waterfall plot" (commonly used in SDR) is.
In that case, each timestep produces a vector containing the FFT of a signal. It falls downward over time.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
<!-- A clear and concise description of what you want to happen. -->
A way to visualize data as a waterfall plot while reducing data duplication.

@Wumpf suggested a special view that could use a range query over all iterations (and data would be logged normally, as its created) ([discord discussion](https://discord.com/channels/1062300748202921994/1372225524818247800))

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
<!-- A clear and concise description of any alternative solutions or features you've considered. -->
We separately log this information in HDF5 files customized for our use case. An HDF5 viewer can view this data as a 2D image, but we lose the ability to scrub and sync up hardware behaviors with other things in the system seamlessly.

Since the main issue is duplication, we could compress the data or use a sliding time window.

**Additional context**
<!-- Add any other context or screenshots about the feature request here. -->
This feature is not by any means crucial for our specific use case.

data.title: Documentation - Using send column api with custom archtypes and components
Support h.264/h.265 b-frames on `VideoStream` archetype

labels.name: feat-video
labels.description: anything video decoding, player, querying, data modelling of videos etc.

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

data.body:
Our `VideoAsset` archetype has no issues with b-frames at all. However, the (as of writing upcoming) `VideoStream` archetype won't support b-frames in its first few iterations.

B-frames for h.264/h.265 create additional complexity as they require differing decode timestamps (DTS) and presentation timestamps (PTS):
We have to add decode timestamps as a separate optional field and take care of the necessary reordering. An additional issue is that currently we assume that all video frames come in-order (rather special as all our other logging it out-of-order!). This greatly complicates access into rerun chunks containing frame data.

As encoders emit b-frames alongside both prior and successive frames, one way to solve this is to extend `VideoStream` to have _arrays_ of presentation time offsets and allow several frames to be in a single sample. This way, the stream of samples is still ordered in decoding order, keeping decoder ingestion simple. Since any use of b-frames naturally causes significant latency, this solution is likely truthful to the actual output.
(Note, that none of the decoders we worked with so far actually needs the actual value of the DTS, so we're not missing this information anywhere!)

See also:
* https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/7484

TODO: What about bframe support on AV1 and VP9? We probably support this fine already, as these codecs don't have the sample ordering issue AVC/HEVC have. But we should test it!
