data.title: Project: ergonomic and unambiguous references to streams/columns of data
data.body:
## Summary description

As part of most workflows, users need refer to data from many different contexts:
- At log-time via our object-APIs
- Via direct schema markup in record-batches
- At query-time
- When building blueprints
- In the viewer

When a user needs to refer to the SAME data across more than one context this presents challenges in making sure they are able to specify this AND that the means of specification is obvious and discoverable.

The inherent challenge here is that forcing the user to fully specify every bit of metadata makes our system too painful to use, but being overly flexible makes it too easy to make mistakes or introduce ambiguities .

The focus of this project is to come up with an approach that hits the right trade-offs, and update our data-model and API surfaces where necessary.

## Background and problem

In the old days it was generally sufficient to refer to data via `(entity_path, component)`.

However, with the the move to [tagged components](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/6889), a user must now specify several additional pieces of information (archetype, field, etc.), and there are increased opportunities for this data to be left partially filled or over-specified.

Additionally, our dataframe APIs have added a further complexity.  When data is mapped into a dataframe or table, we must give it a column name. Most integrations optimize this column name as the most canonical way of referring to the data. Often time the metadata isn't even visible in default table-printers.

There are two aspects of this work:
- If a user adds data to the same dataset via two different mechanisms.  (e.g. once via logged objects and once via converted chunks), are the specifiers recognized as matching by the system in the way that this data ends up merged together as the same logical stream/column.
- If a user adds data to a dataset, and then wishes to query for that data, are they able to easily construct the specifier they need in the query or blueprint.

## Grounding use-cases
<!-- Rerun is both powerful and complex, which makes it easy to go off and solve abstract problems that don't actually provide significant value in any realistic scenarios.

This section should describe the real world use-cases that the project is targeting.

If this project has significant user experience implications,
this section should likely link to some more thorough user research.

NOTE: take care to not put any proprietary user-information here or in any publicly accessible place. Any such information should be properly secured in private locations. Any information that the user's have publicly shared themselves is fine to link to.
-->
- A user creates a dataset via logging APIs, and then wants to query it
  - How do they specify which column(s) they want to access?
    - Our current view contents is specified as, e.g. `{"world/cameras/**": ["ImageBuffer", "PinholeProjection"]}` but this does not let us specify archetypes/fields.
    - Once mapped to datafusion, how do they write a `.select(...)` this generally requires passing the column name to datafusion.
- A user creates a table with sorbet annotations and then sends it to the viewer:
  - How are the columns named?
  - If there is both a name and an entity path, which do we show? How do they discover the other?
  
- TODO: Add more as needed 

## How to describe, demo and evaluate
<!-- This section will vary significantly depending on the type of project.

- How should the output of this project be described (docs, blogpost)?
- How do we best demo the result (new code examples, demo videos, before/after metrics)
- How do we evaluate success (target benchmark, target use-case requires much less code, user interviews)?
-->
TODO

## Designs and plans
<!-- Any notes or material on the design and implementation plans -->
TODO

data.title: LatestAt queries need a mechanism to provide the context of the origin time

labels.name: feat-dataframe-api
labels.description: Everything related to the dataframe API

data.body:
### Context
LatestAt queries are very powerful, but they currently materialize data somewhat magically, without  providing a mechanism to actually know where that data came from. This can be important for use-cases like:
- Doing additional queries at that specific time-point once you know "when" something happened.
  - A common pattern is for a user to log "events" when interesting things happen. It's easy to write a query that finds the last instance of an event before a particular time. But once you find the event you have no way of knowing when the event actually happened.
- Understanding how old data is relative to the query time
- Implementing interpolation functions

### Example
Probably best articulated with an example.

Consider the table:
```
+----------+------------+-----------+
| log_tick | /my_scalar | /my_color |
+----------+------------+-----------+
|    1     |   1.2      |   RED     |
|    3     |   3.4      |    -      |
|    5     |   2.7      |   BLUE    |
|    7     |   4.1      |    -      |
+----------+------------+-----------+
```

When using `fill_latest_at()` it can be helpful to be able to answer the question: "From which time was the latest_at data filled it".

It should be possible to do something like the following:
```python
dataset.dataframe_query_view(index="log_tick", contents="/**")
       .using_index_values([4, 10])
       .fill_latest_at(with_origin_time=True)
       .df()
       .select("log_tick",
               "/my_scalar",
               "/my_scalar:log_tick",
               "/my_color",
               "/my_color:log_tick")
```

Or maybe only materialize these on-demand if there was a way to articulate this as a udf?
```python
dataset.dataframe_query_view(index="log_tick", contents="/**")
       .using_index_values([4, 10])
       .fill_latest_at()
       .df()
       .select("log_tick",
               "/my_scalar",
               udf.origin_time("/my_scalar"),
               "/my_color",
               udf.origin_time("/my_color"))
```

The expected output would be:
```
+----------+------------+---------------------+-----------+---------------------+
| log_tick | /my_scalar | /my_scalar:log_tick | /my_color | /my_color:log_tick  |
+----------+------------+---------------------+-----------+---------------------+
|    4     |   3.4      |          3          |   RED     |          1          |
|   10     |   4.1      |          7          |   BLUE    |          5          |
+----------+------------+---------------------+-----------+---------------------+
```

data.title: Explore GStreamer based video decoding (at least for h264/h265)

labels.name: user-request
labels.description: This is a pressing issue for one of our users

labels.name: feat-video
labels.description: anything video decoding, player, querying, data modelling of videos etc.

data.body:
Our current ffmpeg exectuable based video decoding is riddled with bugs and performance issues. Several people pointed out to us that it should be relatively easy to _installed gstreamer binaries_ with [gstream-rs](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/gstreamer/gstreamer-rs) (thus sidestepping most license issues). Unlike the older Rust ffmpeg binding library this is relatively easy to use.

For specific (!!) gstreamer versions, known hardware configuration and renderer, we should be able to even copy directly gpu decoded images to our textures, allowing much faster decoding. Since our decoder interface already works with wgpu textures (in order to support WebCodec) better, we're already in a great spot for this (in fact we only read back hovered pixels for interaction!)

In short, the motivation is:
* better performance - we want to be able to decode & seek several 4k videos
* sidestep various bugs we have with ffmpeg executable playback
* more formats quicker (h265 should be possible with the ffmpeg executable approach but may need some extra work, others will be harder!)

Since we still have the ffmpeg decoder around (no need to remove it if we don't want to) we're perfectly fine with feature restrictions like no b-frame support (as long as we fall back dynamically), which are exceedingly uncommon in robotics streaming cases as they obviously add a lot of latency.

data.title: Sub-plots within the TimeSeries view
data.body: ## Background Axis-aligned stacks of plot is a widely requested feature for which there exists no convenient workaround. #7931 proposes a somewhat generic mechanism to "synchronise" axes between multiple views, in hope to benefit from the layout flexibility of our view system. The present issue is a counter-proposal based on the (admittedly somewhat subjective) observation that the view system is too rigid and abstract for this purpose, and that a pragmatic, "sub-plots-within-a-view" approach would provide the same/similar results with lower complexity, both in UX design and code. ## Proposal The core proposal is to allow multiple plots in a grid _within the same timeseries view_, à la matplotlib's subplots (currently, a view can only contain a single plot). Also, within these sub-plots, any "facing"" axes would automatically be linked and aligned, without a possibility to opt-out (rationale: limit the number of configuration option + use the view system if you want loosely coupled plots). ## Challenges - Design of the UI to configure the plot view (see proposal below) - Design of the blueprint APIs (in particular, how the "entity path filter" mini-language fits in the picture - Implementation: - egui_plot needs quite a bit of cleanup work - can the multi-plot layout—and alignement!—be done outside of egui_plots? ## UX proposal The core proposal consists of a "mini-map" of the plot layout where entities can be dragged and dropped to the desired sub-plot. By default, there is a single subplot, and all entities produced by the entity path filter are assigned to it: An entity would be removed by filtering it out from the entity path filter. The user would click on the + icons to create further rows/column of subplots, and then drag-and-drop entity to dispatch them to the desired sub-plot: Alternative to the + buttons: a couple of fields to enter the desired number of rows and columns. ### Stretch goal 1: assign "weight" to columns or row (This is probably too janky of a UI and better done by dragging some kind of boundary between sub-plots.) See **[designs in Figma](https://www.figma.com/design/72AuvfbssFJeqqnQoJscYT/Katya-s-playground?node-id=5630-8588&t=J2SqZnOtoZyKvDMY-1)** for this as well ### Stretch goal 2: optionally assign an entity one or more of the X axes An area would be displayed at the bottom of each column, in which case that entity would be used as abscissa instead of time values. This of course would require some time alignement for all scalars involved, but this is typically the case anyways. For such plot, the time cursor would be displayed as a marker highlighting the corresponding points, as opposed to a vertical line. ## Related - [figjam board](https://www.figma.com/board/SOw7dU1ZETrBaShqA2NPPp/HMW?node-id=0-1&t=ma6VGs0mFG4DT8dP-1) with the above graphics and the original drawings from Nov 2024 meet-up - [Figma sketches](https://www.figma.com/design/72AuvfbssFJeqqnQoJscYT/Katya-s-playground?node-id=5630-8588&t=J2SqZnOtoZyKvDMY-1) - https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/7931 - https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/8286 - https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/2240 - https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/294

**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**  
I’m working with large E57 files, where a single file can contain multiple scans, each with millions of points. Loading the entire file into `rerun` just to visualize or debug a small subset is not feasible due to memory and performance constraints. Currently, `rerun` loads all points from the file via external data loader plugin, which significantly slows down workflows with large datasets. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**  
I’d like `rerun`’s external data loader plugins to support parameters that allow passing inputs, filters or other information to the plugin. In my case, this could be in the form of scan indices, IDs, or metadata filters passed into the loader, enabling partial loading of only the necessary scans.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**  
- Splitting E57 files manually into separate scans, but this adds preprocessing complexity and increases storage usage.  
- Passing environmental variables to select scans like `RERUN_E57_DISPLAY_SCANS=0,1,5,10 rerun ../../pointcloud/engine_room.e57`. It works from command line, but not a real solution.

data.title: create `PyRemoteTask` to model redap asynchronous tasks in the PythonSDK

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

data.body:
### Context

The dataplatform introduced asynchronous tasks to run long running operations, such as partitions indexing, etc - original (read: possibly outdated) [design doc](https://www.notion.so/rerunio/RFC-Async-task-execution-in-the-dataplatform-1abb24554b19808bbae3e6a4bd483f7c).

The first such operation using the new model is `RegisterWithDataset` (see: https://github.com/rerun-io/dataplatform/pull/543). 

In https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/pull/9590, we have merged a stop-gap change to keep the `register` python sdk API synchronous by having it secretly call the "query_tasks_on_completion` (aka wait) method after having issued a registration.

This has problems, including:
* we have hard-coded a maximum and arbitrary wait time of 1 minute, which means that the call would break if anything takes longer than a minute.
* it defeats the purpose of having the asynchronous API, if the client needs to block anyway.


### What

Create a pythonic way to use the asynchronous API. Asynchronous endpoints should return something like a `PyRemoteTask` that offers methods such as `id()`, `status()` or `wait_for_completion()`.

Optionally, we should also consider adding explicitly blocking methods, that some customers may prefer to use, especially in interactive context (python shell, notebooks): for example: `register_blocking(path, max_blocking_time)`

data.title: Refactor `TimeInt` vs `NonMinI64` vs `i64`

labels.name: 😤 annoying
labels.description: Something in the UI / SDK is annoying to use

labels.name: 🚜 refactor
labels.description: Change the code, not the functionality

data.body:
We store our time values as `i64`, but we reserve `i64::MIN` as a special value that we _sometimes_ use to indicate static data. This has lead us into what feels like over-engineering with a bunch of types:

* `NonMinI64` - the set of valid time values
* `TimeInt` - either the special `STATIC` (`i64::MIN`) or a valid `NonMinI64`
* `i64` - how data is actually stored in arrow

At the same time, we convert between these types so often that we have a bunch of `.into()` that just does saturating casts.

I'm pretty sure we're using `TimeInt` in a lot of places where we _should_ be using `NonMinI64`.

What can we do to simplify this situation?

Should we replace it all with `i64`?

data.title: Can't use arrow datatype `Duration` with `datafusion 46`
data.body:
## Problem
Datafusion 46 does not support the `Duration` datatype:

> Internal error: Min/Max accumulator not implemented for type Duration(Nanosecond).

This is fixed on Datafusion trunk:

* https://github.com/apache/datafusion/pull/15322

Which will be released maybe mid April (1-3 weeks away):

* https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/15072

## Where are we using `datafusion`
We're not, not directly, but `lance` is, and it's using `datafusion` 45.0.0

## Solutions
### Wait
Wait for a new datafusion release:
* https://github.com/apache/datafusion/issues/15072

…and then wait for `lance` to update. This may take a while.

### Avoid `Duration` datatype
We could avoid using the `Duration` datatype until the next datafusion/lance releases.

If we do, we should wait with the Rerun 0.23 release until then as well, which may well be a month away.

### Patch `datafusion` in dataplatform
Use a patched `datafusion` version (e.g. on our own fork) in crates.io.

We could still hit the problem when using da an old datafusion from Python though.

data.title: FileSink does not cause python unit tests to fail on errors
data.body:
**Describe the bug**

If you have an error that occurs during `spawn_and_stream` it gets logged as an error on the terminal *but* it the process returns successfully. This can cause unit test to succeed when they otherwise should fail.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Change the method `write_arrow_to_bytes` in `crates/store/re_log_encoding/src/codec/arrow.rs` to immediately return an error.
2. Build normally.
3. Run unit test `test_roundtrip_send` in `rerun_py/tests/unit/test_dataframe.py`
4. Unit test succeeds because we do not raise any assertions from the spawned task errors only being reported to the terminal

**Expected behavior**

An error message in the terminal should cause unit tests to fail.

**Additional context**

A proof of concept solution to this is below.I have changed two lines, using `capfd` fixture and the final assert to make sure "ERROR" doesn't occur in stderr. There is an open question as to whether warnings should also cause unit test failures.

If implemented, we would want to this across most or all of our py unit tests.

```python
    def test_roundtrip_send(self, capfd) -> None:
        df = self.recording.view(index="my_index", contents="/**").select().read_all()

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
            rrd = tmpdir + "/tmp.rrd"

            with rr.RecordingStream("rerun_example_test_recording") as rec:
                rec.save(rrd)
                rr.dataframe.send_dataframe(df, rec=rec)

            round_trip_recording = rr.dataframe.load_recording(rrd)

        df_round_trip = round_trip_recording.view(index="my_index", contents="/**").select().read_all()

        print("df:")
        print(df)
        print()

        print("df_round_trip:")
        print(df_round_trip)
        print()

        assert df == df_round_trip

        assert "ERROR" not in capfd.readouterr().err
```

Perhaps one or more of the following could be implemented:

Apologies if some of the suggestions don't make sense, I am not as familiar with the architecture of Rerun.

data.title: Consider using Link-Time Optimization (LTO) for the project
data.body:
Hi!

I noticed that for some reason, Link-Time Optimization (LTO) is not enabled in the project. I tried to find any discussion about it in the repo (like other issues) but didn't find anything about that question.

Is there any specific reason for not using LTO for the project? Since Rerun is a huge one, with LTO we can significantly improve binary sizes and allow the compiler to perform more aggressive cross-crate optimizations. If FatLTO is too expensive to run even for releases we can consider "cheaper" from build resources perspective option - ThinLTO (though it's less efficient than FatLTO from performed optimizations perspective). Other options like `codegen-units = 1` also will help with more aggressive optimizations.

I think you can enable LTO only for the Release builds so as not to sacrifice the developers' experience while working on the project, since LTO consumes an additional amount of time to finish the compilation routine. In this case, we can create a dedicated `[profile.optimized-dev]` profile where LTO will be disabled (so developers experience will not be affected).

I performed some tests with the build command from the Pixi file for building binaries in the Release mode. Test env: Fedora 41, AMD Ryzen 9 5900x, specified in the project settings Rustc version.

Binary size results:

Rerun CLI:

* Release: 105 Mib
* Release + `codegen-units = 1` + ThinLTO: 95 Mib
* Release + `codegen-units = 1` + FatLTO: 85 Mib

Rerun WASM:

* Release: 39 Mib
* Release + `codegen-units = 1` + ThinLTO: 33 Mib
* Release + `codegen-units = 1` + FatLTO: 33 Mib

The same level of improvements is expected for other project's Rust-based binaries like the Python SDK too.

Clean build times results:

Rerun CLI:

* Release: 1m 52s
* Release + `codegen-units = 1` + ThinLTO: 3m 01s
* Release + `codegen-units = 1` + FatLTO: 6m 34s

Rerun WASM:

* Release: 65s
* Release + `codegen-units = 1` + ThinLTO: 97s
* Release + `codegen-units = 1` + FatLTO: 97s

Thank you.

data.title: Fallback provider are unable to provide arrays of fallback (in practice)
data.body:
Let's first have a look at a one of the - seemingly rare - usecases:
SeriesLines/SeriesPoints should provide an individual color for each of its series. How many series are available is determined at execution time of the visualizer.
An explicit non-example worth calling out is the visibility property of SeriesLines/SeriesPoints: while we allow individual series to be invisible on a single entity, this value can be spatted accross all series so it doesn't need to be an array fallback!

In theory fallback providers can provide arbitrary arrow arrays as fallbacks
However, in practice there's a bunch of hurdles:
* knowing how many values to produce is hard to pipe through, the best bet today is to pass it through via the view state but that's quite inelegant
* `TypedComponentFallbackProvider` are all about single values  which is convenient for the most part. Can we extend the trait to also provide arrays without too much overhead?

labels.name: feat-video
labels.description: anything video decoding, player, querying, data modelling of videos etc.

data.body: I am capturing high-speed video at 120fps that is encoded into H.264 (avc1.4D4020) MP4 files. I am able to log the video file in Rerun, but the video will not display in a native viewer on Mac, Ubuntu Linux, or Windows (the video window will just display a spinning circle and will not load the video image). The video will display in the web Rerun viewer on Chrome and Firefox. **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Log a 120 fps H.264 (avc1.4D4020) encoded MP4 video file in rerun with the AssetVideo interface. Python code: # Log the video in rerun with timestamps video_asset = rr.AssetVideo(path=video_filepath) rr.log(f"video_{video_index}", video_asset, static=True) # Get the internal video frame timestamps frame_timestamps_ns = video_asset.read_frame_timestamps_ns() rr.send_columns( f"video_{video_index}", # Note timeline values don't have to be the same as the video timestamps. indexes=[rr.TimeNanosColumn("timeline", frame_timestamps_ns)], columns=rr.VideoFrameReference.columns_nanoseconds(frame_timestamps_ns), ) 2. Launch a native Rerun viewer. **Expected behavior** The video should load normally in a rerun window and the user should be able to seek to arbitrary location in the video's timeline. **Screenshots** **Backtrace** N/A **Desktop (please complete the following information):** - OS: MacOS Sonoma 14.74, ffmpeg version 7.0 & 7.11 - Hardware: Apple Silicon MacBook M3 Pro - OS: Linux Ubuntu 22.04, ffmpeg version N-118350-ge20ee9f9ae - Hardware: PC - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X 16-core 4.3 Ghz Processor, 96 GB RAM, 4TB Samsung SSD 990 PRO, GeForce RTX 4090 24 GB Graphics Card **Rerun version** 0.22.0 **Additional context** - Behavior confirmed by @Wumpf on his Windows Rerun viewer. - It looks like the number of i-frames in the video affects how it is rendered in the native Rerun video. The original video was encoded with a GOP (Group Of Pictures) size of 60000, meaning there was only one i-frame in the original video I tested. - I tried further tests with videos encoded with a GOP of 120 (1 i-frame per second of video) and 60 (2 i-frames per second of video). These videos displayed better in the native Rerun viewer on Linux Ubuntu 22.04 with ffmpeg version N-118350-ge20ee9f9ae. There was a little stuttering in the video with GOP of 120 and almost no stuttering with GOP of 60. But in the Mac Rerun viewer the video would display single still frames, but not play the video smoothly.

data.title: Project: User-defined recording properties
data.body:
<!--
Projects are larger (~2+ person-weeks) pieces of work that have a beginning and an end.
This issue is meant to be used to track a single project through conception to shipped.

A project issue doesn't need to be fully filled out in the beginning of the project but must be at the time of shipping.

Feel free to add any helpful sections to make it as useful as possible to the team running the project and as clear as possible for anyone else. Also feel free to move around sections if you think it fits better.
-->

## Summary description
<!-- A clear and concise (summary) description of what this project is about .-->

Enable users to assign custom properties to a recording, as well as registering currently hardcoded information (such as `application_id`, name of a recording) late during the logging process.

## Background and problem
<!-- Describe the background to why we want to do this project and what problem we're trying to solve-->

It is very common for the user to have properties (metadata) that they want to associate with a recording—some of this information might only be available at the end of the recording. Examples of this could be _"How was the weather?"_, or _"Was the task in this episode executed correctly?"_.

Right now, we only provide very limited, or hardcoded bits of information, such as `application_id` and `started` time. It's important to note that the this aforementioned information is not part of any Arrow `RecordBatch` making it inaccessible for the dataplatform to index.

## Grounding use-cases
<!-- Rerun is both powerful and complex, which makes it easy to go off and solve abstract problems that don't actually provide significant value in any realistic scenarios.

This section should describe the real world use-cases that the project is targeting.

If this project has significant user experience implications,
this section should likely link to some more thorough user research.

NOTE: take care to not put any proprietary user-information here or in any publicly accessible place. Any such information should be properly secured in private locations. Any information that the user's have publicly shared themselves is fine to link to.
-->

1. The user wants to assign a name (such as _"Episode 42"_) to the recording that shows up in the viewer instead of the timestamp that we currently use as an item below the application id in the recording panel.
2. The user wants to gain quick insights, such as camera information, from a recording by hovering over a recording name (without the need for switching to that recording).
3. The user wants to assign tags to recordings (like `rainy`, `cloudy`, ...) to a recording. The dataplatform will be able to pick up these tags and show them as properties in a catalog view, and use them to create derived views (all recordings where weather was `rainy`) to feed into training pipelines.
4. The user can assign complex information (semantic information that exceeds string-based key-value pairs), such as thumbnails, to a recording directly from the SDK, something that does not work via the dataplatform CLI and currently requires implementing a custom gRPC client.
5. The users can evolve their recording properties over time, adding additional information when needed, while maintaining backwards compatibility.

## How to describe, demo and evaluate
<!-- This section will vary significantly depending on the type of project.

- How should the output of this project be described (docs, blogpost)?
- How do we best demo the result (new code examples, demo videos, before/after metrics)
- How do we evaluate success (target benchmark, target use-case requires much less code, user interviews)?
-->

* Recording properties show up in the selection panel and in tooltips.
* Show how users can query the dataplatform for interesting recordings.
* Large datasets (such as LeRobot) in the _Recording Panel_ will look much more organized recording names
* Demo how users can rename recordings live via the logging SDK.
* Provide examples in all SDKs that make use of this new functionality.

## Designs and plans
<!-- Any notes or material on the design and implementation plans -->

Overall, the goal is to move as much information as possible to Sorbet-compliant record batches that the dataplatform directly knows how to handle (for querying and indexing). That means we have to move over information that is currently sent via gRPC headers (`StoreInfo`) into `Chunks`. The key issue that will unlock this is:

* #8776.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Changing `SetStoreInfo` is a breaking change that we ideally want to make before the `v0.23` release, as we are already breaking backwards compatibility there.

Another big advantage of moving information to the `Chunks` is that we can evolve their definitions via Sorbet's backwards compatibility mechanisms and test for breaking changes.

Here is a list of design decisions for modeling the new feature:

* We send recording properties to a reserved entity path (something like `/_properties`) as static data.
* Properties are send as a regular chunk—our SDKs make sure to send this chunk early, but crucially not part of the `SetStoreInfo` message.
* Blueprints also need to have (at minimum) a chunk that contains `/_properties` with an `application_id`. The construction of that chunk is done internally by the SDK.
* The points above mean that `application_id` can change late, in which case the viewer creates a new application in the recording panel, but (for now) that new application won't have a blueprint associated with it (because the application_ids don't match any more).
* In the SDKs we provide a helper function (something like `rr.set_recording_properties(/* as components */)`) to hide the reserved entity path and help with discoverability.

Here is a plan on how to bring this to fruition:

* Provide a shim around the current `StoreInfo`.
* We have to change the StoreHub to notify (`SetSelection`) the viewer when recordings are (partially) ready because they have an `application_id`.
* The EntityDb::store_info calls to get `application_id` and started will be replaced by a `EntityDb::properties` call that queries all `/_properties` using `latestAt`.

### Challenges

* Tight coupling of blueprint with `application_id` and `store_id`.
* Current implementation of the _Welcome screen_ is tacked onto that concept.
* No defined chunk in which recording properties appear make registering a recording with the viewer more complex.

## Tasks
<!-- Tasks needed to complete the project -->

Most concrete tasks are defined as sub issues below.

## Non-goals and won't do
<!-- Any clarifications of related problems this project won't tackle -->

This issue won't tackle adding information to existing/closed recordings, which will be done in a follow-up project.

data.body:
Connected to https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/349

**Describe the bug**
Transforms between 2D spaces is rather useful, e.g. `/camera` is full res image but `/camera/segmentation` was done at lower res. It works well for segmentation images and bounding boxes by logging a Transform3D (yay!) but the labels of the bounding boxes are not affected by the transform

```
import numpy as np

rr.init("test", spawn=True)

# Draw random 2D boxes

    rr.Boxes2D(
        array=rects + 10,
        array_format=rr.Box2DFormat.XYXY,
        colors=np.asarray([255, 255, 0],dtype=np.uint8),
        labels=["in world"] * count,
    ),
)

# Scale transform between 2D worlds
rr.log("/world/boxes", rr.Transform3D(scale=0.5))
rr.log(
    "/world/boxes",
    rr.Boxes2D(
        array=rects,
        array_format=rr.Box2DFormat.XYWH,
        colors=np.asarray([255, 0, 0,],dtype=np.uint8),
        labels=["in world/boxes"] * count,
    ),
)
```
The red labels are shown correctly in the `world/boxes` view but incorrectly in the `world` view.

**Expected behavior**

data.title: Move `store_source` and `store_version` from `StoreInfo` into `archetypes::RecordingProperties`
Project: first-class stateless API for the Python SDK
data.body:
## Summary description

Currently, the first-class Python API is the stateful one (`rr.init()`, `rr.log()`, etc.). It has however several problems:

* It's bad for elaborate scenario, in particular when many recording streams are involved
* It diverge from the Rust and C++ SDKs
* The stateful implementation is hard to maintain, in particular because it is buried in the rust implementation.
* Discoverability is [much better](https://rerunio.slack.com/archives/C033K5VS2KD/p1751973989181989?thread_ts=1751926135.772189&cid=C033K5VS2KD) with a stateless API 

The stateless api (`rec = rr.new_recording()`, `rec.log()`, etc.) doesn't suffer from these issues. This project is about make these first class.

Notes:

* This project is not about *removing* the stateful API, but making it second-class to the *stateless* one.
* This project is related to, but does not include the [stateless time APIs](#3841).

## Background and problem

The current situation is as follows:

* The rust python binding maintains the notion of "current recording", on which the stateful APIs hinge.
* On python side, the stateful API is first-class in the sense that it implements the actual logic (the core aspect of which is delegated to the rust bindings), and is prominently displayed in our docs/examples.
* The stateful APIs (aka methods of `RecordingStream` simply delegate to the stateful ones, passing `recording=self`. Until recently, this was done via monkey patching, which was really bad for LSPs (fixed by [#9182](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/9182)).

Problems:

* The "current recording" logic is deep into the implementation.
* The rust bindings have significant complexity over the Rust native `RecordingStream`.
* This entire thing is generally hard to maintain.
* See the other issues listed at the top.

## Desired outcome

* The core Python API surface is the `RecordingStream` object.
* The python `RecordingStream` object is entirely implemented in Rust, and it's implementation is a thin shim over the Rust-native `RecordingStream`.
* The stateful API is relegated to a separate, pure Python module which maintains the current recording as a Python global variable.
* The stateful APIs no longer have a `recording` argument. They always apply to the "current recording". If you want a `recording` argument, you actually want the stateless API.
* Opinionated stretch goal: using the stateful api requires a specific import (e.g. `import rerun.stateful as rrs`). This mirrors matplotlib behaviour (`import matplotlib.pyplot as plt`).
* Many/all examples/snippets/docs are updated to use the stateless API.

## Tasks

[#9182](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/9182) was a small step in that direction. Here are the next ones:

- [ ] Move the implementation logic to `RecordingStream` and delegate to that in the stateful API calls.
- [ ] Remove `rr.new_recording` in favour or `RecordingStream.__init__()`.
- [ ] Remove the `recording: RecordingStream | None = None` argument from the stateful APIs.
- [ ] Address the highly verbose docstring duplication between the stateful and stateless APIs.
  - Since the stateful APIs no longer have a `recording` parameter, they are identical to the stateless one (minus `self`, which is generally not documented), so maybe there is a way to duplicate the docstring in code in a way that makes LSP happy.
  - Failing that, we revert to shortening the stateful docstrings to a minimum, merely referencing the stateless counterparts.
- [ ] Re-implement `RecordingStream` in rust, as a thin wrapper over the rust-native `RecordingStream`
- [ ] (Opinionated stretch goal) Relegate the stateful API in a dedicated namespace
- [ ] Update documentation/snippets/example to emphasis the stateless API

## Non-goals and won't do

This project doesn't not cover the stateless *time* API (but things will sure look great once both efforts are completed).

## Related

* [https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/2158](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/2158)
* [https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/2116](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/2116)
* [https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/3978](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/3978)
* [https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/6420](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/6420)
* [https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/3743](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/3743)
* [https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/8023](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/8023)
* [https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/3841](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/3841)
* [https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/pull/9182](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/pull/9182)

data.title: Performance Issues for visible time range set to beginning / end of timeline
data.body:
**Describe the bug**
Adding any data (except Scalar) with a time component will result in a major performance hit when the time range is "big enough" or in my case fully displayed. Also adding a time stamp somehow increases the data size by 5x.

**To Reproduce**
The following script will produce two 2D point clouds of same size. The first will be put in "fast" and just add the point cloud with one time point. The second one is called "slow" and will give every point a time. To see the described effect, you have to override the visible time range. 
```
import rerun as rr
import numpy as np

N= 100_000
times = np.linspace(0, 1, N)
xy = np.random.rand(N, 2)

rr.init("test", recording_id="fast", spawn=True)
rr.set_time_seconds("sensor_time", times[0])
rr.log(
    "data",
    rr.Points2D(
        xy,
        colors=[(255, 255, 255)],
    ),
)

rr.init("test", recording_id="slow", spawn=True)
rr.send_columns(
    "data",
    indexes=[rr.TimeSecondsColumn("sensor_time", times)],
    columns=[*rr.Points2D.columns(positions=xy)]
)
```

**Expected behavior**
My expectation was, that the performance should stay the same, since the same number of points is displayed. I suspect that adding a timestamp somehow causes an additional query to happen. I also do not understand why the datasize increases by a factor of 5, since we're only adding one more column (time) to the dataset.

data.title: Automated tool to detect version-breaking changes in our .fbs files
data.body:
* Follows https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/8748
* See also [this notion doc](https://www.notion.so/rerunio/Track-Stable-formats-3e39ef8300424aee90cdf161933ba805?pvs=4)

Whenever we change something in an .fbs file we should try to do so in a way that is backwards compatible.

If an edit is NOT backwards compatible, the CI should catch it and tell you.

## Backwards and forwards compatible changes
* Adding nullable struct fields (older versions should ignore unknown fields)
* Adding new enum variant (older versions should ignore unknown variants)
* Marking enum or struct fields as deprecated
* Changing the _name_ of an enum variant (but keeping its numerical value) (should be fine?)
* …?

## Incompatible changes
* Fully removing enum/struct fields
* Adding a required struct field
* Changing a struct field datatype
* Changing the name of a struct field
* Changing the numeric value of an enum variant
* Changing a struct to an enum (or vsv)
* …?

## Related proejcts
* For datatype generics: https://docs.rs/narrow/latest/narrow/

data.title: Design a scalable approach to "viewer/blueprint commands"
data.body:
We have a desire to trigger certain actions from our SDK that affects the viewer directly:
* Activate blueprint $ID
* Open/close recording $ID
* Play/pause/move time cursor
* …

So far, only a few of these have been implemented, and in rather ad-hoc ways:
* https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/pull/8809/files
* https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/blob/026d84622c054de3159646667a9d35c90e361e9f/crates/store/re_protos/proto/rerun/v0/log_msg.proto#L16-L17

## Where can we send these commands?
* From the logging SDKs (Python, Rust, C++)
* From Python notebooks (via logging SDK)
* From JS API ? 

### Blueprint changes
Some of these commands can be encoded as changes to the blueprint store.
This include setting the time state, once [this is part of the blueprint](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/8318).

Changes to blueprint can be implemented as any other store changes, i.e. by pushing a chunk (recordbatch).
Similarly, querying the blueprint state ("what is the time cursor at?") can be implemented as a data query.

## Design
None yet, but it would be nice with something _data driven_, e.g. a protobuf definition of all commands as an `oneof`.

## Related issues
* https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/7728
* https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/8318

data.title: `ffmpeg-cli` & Safari `WebCodec` decoder requires additional frames enqueued for some videos in order to produce frames + spurious errors

labels.name: feat-video
labels.description: anything video decoding, player, querying, data modelling of videos etc.

data.body:
Some video material, for instance https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/726c1803-9b4b-4dfb-a6ee-29a23a2353a9
(source https://huggingface.co/datasets/pollen-robotics/apple_storage) requires us to enqueue up to 16 more video samples than what expect.
Practically what happens is that as we keep queuing in GOPs/samples, we eventually get frames from ffmpeg, but with a 16 frame delay - i.e. we never get the frames back that we'd expect under normal circumstances.

Note that our WebCodec implementation has no issues with this video in Firefox & Chrome. **However**, the sample issue arises on Safari!

As of [TODO PR LINK] we now make sure that we have at least 16 samples enqueued for the ffmpeg cli decoder at any point in time to work around this.

---

Furthermore, even with a more aggressive enqueuing strategy that takes this into account we are seeing spurious errors like these which recover either after rendering more frames.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/251b21c1-0b00-4c7d-b9fd-366dd9e2775d)
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ead82ced-d6f5-4cdf-89d6-93f1a6c5bc1f)

It also has been observed that when viewing several of these videos at once errors only disappear after seeking:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee5f781b-3552-4f01-96d4-72d4185d04f1)

---

As of now it's unclear what is different about this video material than others we tried in the past. The video example linked above is an "easy" case: It has only GOPs with length 2, each consisting of an IDR frame (marked as such both in the NAL header & mp4 container) and a P frame. Did not find any special properties in the SPS (also looked into parsing the PPS but didn't succeed).

Already experimented among other things with....
* various flags to ffmpeg to reduce latency further or override timings
* insert `EndStream`/`EndStream` NAL units at the end of GOPs
* inserting sleeps to feed ffmpeg slower
* insert fill data on stdin
* convert to h264 and back to mp4 with ffmpeg - both play fine and no change if done with copy flags to avoid re-encoding (this should exclude most mp4 specific issues, but note that the AVCC box holding PPS & SPS should be completely replicated)
* extract single frames to image with ffmpeg works fine
* other video players handle this just fine (tried Windows Media Player, VLC, Firefox, Chrome)

Things we should still look into:
* try to build our own "problematic video" in order to understand better what causes these issues (notably the video was chunked from a larger video)
* read-up more on WebCodec implementation in Firefox & Chrome -> prototype with directly interfacing libav
* ?

data.title: Get rid of wasm-bindgen patching shenanigans

labels.name: 🕸️ web
labels.description: regarding running the viewer in a browser

data.body:
`wasm-bindgen` produces a JS file (`re_viewer.js` in our case) which stores the Wasm module and its *linear memory* in a global variable. That global variable is then re-used for every instace of the `WebViewer`, meaning all `WebViewer` instances actually share memory. Normally that is fine, but it breaks down if we have multiple instances of `WebViewer` on the same page ([rerun.io/docs](), and technically also [rerun.io/viewer]()). Additionally, there is no way to deinitialize the memory used by the stored module. This is a problem whenever we start and stop `WebViewer` instances frequently, such as in notebooks. Related issue in `wasm-bindgen`: * [https://github.com/rustwasm/wasm-bindgen/issues/3130]() We currently use a JS script to post-process the output of `wasm-bindgen`: [https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/blob/b926e958da2f62fb73b35864b268cac545ebe52e/rerun_js/web-viewer/build-wasm.mjs#L44-L53]() This wraps the entire module in an exported function, turning all global variables into upvalues. We can call the exported function multiple times to re-initialize those global variables for each instance of `WebViewer`.
The exported function also returns a `deinit` function which may be used to break all references to the Wasm module and its linear memory, effectively freeing it (though the actual freeing may happen later, depending on GC pressure). The script is written such that it can only ever be reliable for a single specific version of `wasm-bindgen`. This is the reason behind the warning. We currently deal with this manually, by running `pixi run js-build-base`, and inspecting the generated output. We have to ensure that the patch continues to do what it's meant to be doing, which is: 1. Wrap the entire generated output in an exported function, allowing separate instances of `WebViewer` to have separate memory. 2. Generate a `deinit` function that correctly breaks all references to the module's memory. These are typically a few cached typed views over the memory, which must also be broken (as otherwise the memory is still reachable through those, and won't ever be GC'd) All of this is pretty gnarly, annoying to deal with, and extremely error prone. ### How do we fix this We have at least two options: * Contribute a proper fix to `wasm-bindgen`. We aren't the only project running into similar issues. This would require communication with the `wasm-bindgen` team and potentially also other projects. * Write better tools for patching and checking if the patch has been applied correctly, including a testing checklist for anyone who has to do it. This checklist would involve testing the initialization and deinitialization of the viewer in various scenarios and configurations, and observing memory usage.

data.title: Make the visualised state of data results more explicit in the UI
data.body:
Consider this view (adapted from the arkit example):
The blueprint tree shows a whole bunch of data results: `/description` and all the `/world/annotations/box-…` ones. The latter appear because they contain a `Text` component, which is visualisable in the text view:

Why, then, only the `/description` data result is being displayed? The full story about this is involved, but boils down to: "visualisers for the `box...` entities have not been automatically created, because these entities do not have a `TextDocumentIndicator` logged (or, in the future, a `TextDocument` archetype tag)". ### Background The determination of a view's content is akin to a funnel: 1) The starting point is the entities present in the store on the current timeline and at the current timepoint. 2) The entity path filter is then applied, which produces a possibly reduced set of candidate entities. (This is what the "Matches 16 entities" note in the first screenshot refers to.) 3) Then, applicability is determined, and only **applicable entities** are kept. An entity is applicable for a given view type if it contains at least all the _required_ components for at least one the the archetype visualisers of that view type. In the case of the text view, the only required component of the only visualiser is `Text`. * in some cases there's also additional criteria on the data like `is_vector` for tensordata in the bar chart 4) The applicable entities are then filtered for "visualizability". Each view class is allowed to decide which entity are **visualizer entities** based on arbitrary view realted criterions. This is very rarely used. One example is the spatial view which will ignore objects which are under a double projections from it's pov. Entities that are visualisable and applicable become **data result** and are displayed in the blueprint tree. In the text view above, there is no applicability filter, and the screenshot shows the 8 visualisable (and thus applicable) entities. 5) Finally, each of the visualisable entities which _also_ contains a matching indicator component is deemed an **indicated entity**. By default, the viewer spawns visualisers _only_ for indicated entities. In the case of the screenshot above, only the `/description` entity is indicated, which explains why it is the only one that is displayed. Notes: - Visualiser can be created and deleted manually. So the _actual_ set of visible entities in a given view can be an arbitrary subset of applicable entities. Only the _default_ set of visible entities corresponds to the indicated entities. For the purpose of this issue, let's call the set of entities for which a visualiser is active the **displayed entities** (but we must find something else for the UI). - Implementation-wise, i'm not 100% sure of the sequencing between steps (3) and (4), but that's beneath the point of this issue. ### Problem Absolutely NONE of the above is made particularly explicit in the UI. Surely we don't need to bubble that much details/complexity, but some consequence of this complexity _is_ visible, and occasionally confusing (even for us!) ### Suggestion Sparingly provide more information on the above, trying to reach a balance between "too many details" and "what the heck is going on here". For example: - Non-displayed data result should be highlighted as such in the blueprint tree (clicking on them is the right first step to create a visualiser). - The view selection panel should provide more information on the above pipeline, e.g.: "16 entities matched, of which 8 are visualisable, of which 1 is displayed" - Come up with proper naming for all of this...

data.title: Project: improved viewer support for table-style data
data.body:
Under development by @jleibs 

## Summary description
Make the viewer work more nicely for table-style data such as data sourced from the recording catalog

## Background and problem

The viewer currently makes fairly deep assumptions that the primary workflow of a user is to understand how 1 or more entities evolve over time.
- By default, views will show all of the entities, but only data for a single time-point for each (unless using range queries). This is efficient when the number of entities is small (see the assorted many-entities performance issues).
- Additionally, the hover/selection model is entity-centric. You can select an inspect an entity. There is no equivalent selection for "index" -- there is always a single time-point implicitly selected by the position of the time cursor.

These assumptions flow all the way into the storage layer -- each entity gets its own parallel data-structure, and our IPC format requires a separate chunk per-entity. Each entity logically exists as one or more columns.

However, this model is at odds with the way users think about some kinds of tabular data. In particular data where we think of the row as "entity-like". For example in a catalog view each row corresponds to a "recording." 

Currently we have two choices for how we think about mapping a table of recordings into the viewer:
1. We can give each recording its own entity-path
  - This totally falls over after a few hundred recordings due to the many-entities problem
  - The dataframe view is effectively useless -- we just end up with a super-wide table and no way to correlated data between recordings
  - But, other views, conceptually work, and you can select a recording and view its user-component-metadata
2. We can use index such as registration time or even just row-id.
  - This has the benefit of working reasonably for the dataframe view
  - However, the timeline view isn't particularly useful
  - There's also no way to "select" a recording
  - The tree shows a hierarchy of "recording properties" rather than a hierarchical organization of recordings
  - Non-table views generally need to be configured to show VisibleTimeRange to make sense or else they only show data associated with a single recording.


## Grounding use-cases
 
Assume we have added Lat/Lon metadata for every recording in our catalog.

Send the catalog of recordings to the viewer:
- Initially view it as a table
- Switch to a map view and see all the recordings as points on the map
- Be able to "select" a single recording

## How to describe, demo and evaluate
<!-- This section will vary significantly depending on the type of project.

- How should the output of this project be described (docs, blogpost)?
- How do we best demo the result (new code examples, demo videos, before/after metrics)
- How do we evaluate success (target benchmark, target use-case requires much less code, user interviews)?
-->
TODO

## Designs and plans
Two possible initial ideas

### Option 1
Expand the types of indexes we support and remove special-casing about temporal/sequential indexing:
- add an "id" index type
- if the index is "id" type, we could default views to show the full index range (need to rename visible time range)
- make it possible to hover/select select a "id" (index-value)
 
### Option 2
More optimizations around a very specific many-entity workflow:
- Introduce a multi-entity chunk where we store entity as a column. (This could be a configuration option chosen at the top-level of a recording).
- This would maybe necessitate an entire alternative store that organized and indexed things differently... not sure if it's possible to ultimately map this to the queries the views do efficiently, or if this would also require more uniform-entity optimizations across views.
- Make the dataframe-view detect this and do the right thing, placing entity values in their own column

## Tasks
<!-- Tasks needed to complete the project -->

- [ ] Simple inline tasks
- [ ] Links to sub-issues

## Non-goals and won't do
<!-- Any clarifications of related problems this project won't tackle -->

Relatedly, we should also persist default blueprint just like we do for active blueprints, so that this sequence of action yields to the expected result: * mess with blueprint * save as default * further mess with blueprint * quit viewer * launch viewer * reload the same recording * => both the active and default blueprint are in the same state as they were upon quitting the viewer Related: * [https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/5670]() * [https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/5640]() * [https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/5692]()

data.title: Documented instructions do not work when using the C++ SDK in a shared library
data.body:
**Describe the bug**
Cannot build a shared library using the the C++ SDK by following the default instructions
since the static library is built without position independent code. 

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Follow these [C++ SDK instructions](https://ref.rerun.io/docs/cpp/stable/md__2home_2runner_2work_2rerun_2rerun_2rerun__cpp_2cmake__setup__in__detail.html#autotoc_md20) and add it to a shared library project
2. Attempt to compile
3. Results in an error since the static library was not compiled with the `-fPIC` flag on

**Fix**
I managed to get things working by compiling from source with the following flags:

```
cmake -B build -S . -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-fpic"
```

I think it's a good idea to either add the flag by default (not sure what the repercussions are) or mention it in the documentation. Happy to look into either and submit a PR.

data.title: Support for MJCF Files

labels.name: 🪵 Log & send APIs
labels.description: Affects the user-facing API for all languages

data.body:
MJCF is a common file format for kinematic robot (and other general physics simulation) descriptions.

It's part of the [MuJoCo](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/latest/modeling.html) physics engine.

Although not as widely used as URDF it has some nice properties and shows up frequently in simulators:
- [Genesis](https://genesis-world.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api_reference/options/morph/index.html)
- [Nvidia Isaac](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/isaacsim/latest/features/environment_setup/ext_omni_isaac_mjcf.html)

At a minimum we should have a reference dataloader implemented in Python or C++ which loads an MJCF project into Rerun by translating to a set of Transforms and Meshes.

However, coercing into the Rerun hierarchy and expanding transforms loses some of the fidelity that could be expressed. This could be a good opportunity to take a look at https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/1533 and think about some form of Viewer-derived joint-space -> Transform conversion leveraging the MJCF model.

In an ideal world a user would be able to publish a single component containing an array of joint-positions at each time stamp and have the robot model fully articulate in the correct way.

data.title: Remove `LogMsg`

labels.name: 🟦 blueprint
labels.description: The data that defines our UI

labels.name: 🪵 Log & send APIs
labels.description: Affects the user-facing API for all languages

data.body:
Currently, all communication between SDK and Viewer is done through `LogMsg`:

https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/blob/3a50bc23ccb9f90083546b69efcb51b063bd830f/crates/store/re_log_types/src/lib.rs#L263-L280

With `LogMsg`, we're mixing a lot of different concerns into one thing. Now that we are migrating our SDK/Viewer comms to gRPC, we can do better. For example:

- An endpoint to acquire the store info for a recording ID, replacing `SetStoreInfo`.
- An endpoint to stream in all chunks from a recording, replacing `ArrowMsg`, and removing the need to pair each chunk with a store ID, because it's implicitly known by the client when opening the stream.
- An endpoint to fetch the blueprint for a recording. This wouldn't have to be streamed at all, so we wouldn't need a `BlueprintActivationCommand` as a "stream end" marker.

On the `rrd` file side, we could:
- Migrate it to only hold one recording, and put `StoreInfo` in the file header, removing the need for `SetStoreInfo`.
- Use a separate file type for blueprints, removing the need for `BlueprintActivationCommand`. We already do this with `.rbl`, but we'd need to actually enforce it.
 
We probably still want multi-recording (including mixed with blueprint) files, but we could wrap these into a "rerun archive" file format, and provide the tools necessary to produce these files, as we currently do with `rerun rrd`.

However, this means adding another user-step of converting to a metadata-preserving format and then manually applying all of the correct  tags.

We should try to reduce this friction where possible

Unlike arrow/polars/datafusion dataframes, which are pure tables with uniform columns, Pandas dataframes have a concrete index, which we could always map to a timeline of the corresponding name.

This could maybe look something like:

```
rr.send_dataframe(df, components=df_components)
```
where the `components` arrray must match the number of columns in the dataframe.

Or maybe with an object-helper similar to AnyValues:
```
rr.send_dataframe(rr.TaggedDataframe(df, df_components))
```

data.title: Arrow schema and metadata tags are lost too easily
data.body:
## Context
Our plan for Sorbet (and tagged components) hinges on being able to reliably "tag" data with semantic information.

The working theory is that every column receives a set of tags:
- path
- archetype
- field
- component

We store these tags in the arrow metadata of the RecordBatch that we send to Rerun, and Rerun uses these tags for everything from driving batching logic to how we visualize the data in the viewer.

## Problem

The problem is it is way way too easy to accidentally lose these tags in most of the arrow libraries.

The reason is fundamental to arrow:
- Arrow Arrays have Datatypes
- Arrow Tables have Fields
- A field is a datatype + a name + a set of metadata (our tags)

As soon as you access a table column:
```python
timestamps = dataset.column("log_time")
positions = dataset.column("/points:Position3D")
```
the metadata is gone.

You now have two bare arrays:
- One of type `List<TimestampNs>`
- One of type `List<List<F32,3>>` 
 
Neither column has tags. No knowledge of the entity path. No knowledge of the components. Not only are they lost, but there's not even a way to store the data on the arrow array.

If you thought you could send this back to arrow
```python
rr.send_dataframe(pa.Table.from_arrays([timestamps, positions])
```
will not do what you want.

You need to manually re-apply the tags at the time that you create the table or else nothing works.

Code to repro:

```python
import rerun as rr

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:

    rr.init("rerun_example_test_recording")

df = recording.view(index="my_index", contents="points").select().read_all()
print(df.schema.field("/points:Position3D").metadata)
```

data.title: Make graphics adapter creation list all adapters one by one and inform why they weren't picked
data.body:
Closely related to:
* spawned by https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/pull/8476
* https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/6581
* https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/7385


Today, we (that's egui) use `request_adapter` to pick a graphics device. That's fine for many usecases, but it would be better if we went through all available adapters one by one using `enumerate_adapters` and list out the reasons why we didn't pick each of them.
The result should be available both on failure case (none is suitable) and on success case (in debug log and upon request in the viewer)

It's tempting to pull out adapter creation entirely out of egui and into re_renderer. However we need to take into account the _surface_ as well:
* this is a strict *requirement* when using WebGL
* on OpenGL & Linux it _helps_ to know the surface because either Vulkan or OpenGL may not be happy with all surfaces

and by doing so we're still bound to surface creation which in turn is tied to window creation

data.title: Dataframe `.select()` API needs some way to error on missing columns

labels.name: feat-dataframe-api
labels.description: Everything related to the dataframe API

data.body:
When we select a column from the dataframe view, we previously made the decision that a missing column would provide results but be implicitly null.

The rationale for this decision was that in many situations, Rerun data producers may not even create a column if something is missing. For example: maybe a detector simply never logs anything if nothing is detected. In these cases, a query-writer reasonably wants a null column to exist.

However, the far, far far more common case is someone exploring the data and writing a test script made a typo. If a user doesn't actually know what was in the dataset, they may think this is validly null data, as opposed to realizing they aren't querying the right content.

We should instead default to error on null, and then provide a mechanism for advanced users to inject any missing-but-required columns into the view only in situations where it makes sense to do so.

data.title: Python/Pixi Dev Improvements
data.body:
### Core problem:
Our python dev experience is still frustrating and causes a lot of friction for developers that aren't familiar with it.

### Some of the sources of pain
1. Maturin interacts with pixi poorly.
    - In particular, creating an editable env triggers a maturin build via rust, which adds an unfortunate amount of overhead at random times for whichever environment includes the rerun-sdk package. This impacts both developer workflows and is a footgun that can lead to very expensive CI jobs that should otherwise be cheap. 
    - Testing of an environment that uses a one-off maturin-built wheel is unnatural (this could be fixed by `pixi build` in the future)
2. We have too many pixi environments and features. This stems from 3 main causes
    - Things which depend on things that are expensive to install (makes bootstrapping the initial pixi environment slow)
    - Things that conflict in weird ways. `cpp` on linux depends on `sysroot_linux-64 = ">=2.17,<3"`, but building `rerun` viewer with that set causes other issues.
    - Things that want to use `source` vs `pypi` versions of the rerun-sdk
3. We have some pixi tasks that don't run as expected, or don't run in the environments you would expect them to use
4. We have tasks that use pixi to run other tasks with different environments
    - This pixi-calling-pixi pattern should work in theory, but it certainly adds to the confusion of what is happening. We should make sure we understand whether we're doing this in a way that is well-defined and that it produces the results we expect.
5. We don't have a defined baseline for "python competency." It's not clear what knowledge we can assume in docs or workflows.

### Proposal 1: Drop (or modify) Maturin
It seems a significant fraction of pain can be tied back to the fact that adding `rerun_py` as an editable package carries a lot of overhead with it. If this were not the case, we wouldn't have a need for a separate `py` environment in the first place, reducing much of the environment proliferation.

I believe for us this looks like creating our own non-maturin-based `pyproject.toml` using a different  tool (maybe hatch?).

This tool should PACKAGE an existing `rerun_bindings.abi3.so`, but for the purposes of creating an editable install should be fine with the fact that it's missing. If `rerun_bindings.abi3.so` is missing from an editable install import time.

We can then introduce a separate pixi task that produces `rerun_bindings.abi3.so` completely outside of any environment-management context that pixi is aware of.

### Proposal 2: Split `examples` into its own pixi project
Our python examples pull in a bunch of dependencies and generally make management of pixi way more involved as well as introducing a ton of overhead in revving the lock-file, etc.

The entire `-pypi` variant of environments and the idea of being able to install the wheel into the environment are also both tied to examples project. This project could still be set up to run against a source build from its parent folder (and would subsequently use the same `rerun_bindings.abi3.so` from Proposal 1, but it wouldn't have any of the other dev-workflow task tooling.

Unit-tests and snippets would both continued to be maintained as part of the top-level project, and any dependencies of unit-tests or snippets would just be part of the base dependencies.

### Proposal 3: Rerun + Pixi Theory of Operation Doc
It's clear we need a bit more than a "type these commands" approach to working with pixi. At least our devs need to understand the basics of how the environments are created, what path-injection machinery is at play, what chain of events happen when you `pixi run` vs `import` from python, etc.

data.title: CI is not properly linting our python code
data.body:
Our CI job:
- https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable_checks_python.yml

Currently runs `pixi run py-lint`

Which lints our code in an environment that's missing the rerun_sdk itself, missing several errors.

These errors are masked by the fact that our  [mypy config](https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/blob/main/.mypy.ini) specifies:
```
ignore_missing_imports = True
```

## What should happen instead
To be the most pedantically correct we should set `ignore_missing_imports = False`

And I believe we should then be running: `pixi run -e examples py-lint` in CI.

However, this is a non-trivial change for two reasons:
- We need to fix the 300 or so lint errors
- Running `pixi run -e py` in CI will trigger pixi to do an editable-install of `rerun_py` which, indirectly kicks off a full rust build of Rerun and the bindings, which will further slow down CI

data.title: Make visualizers & archetypes map 1:1 (+notes on visualizer selection in world without indicators)

labels.name: 🟦 blueprint
labels.description: The data that defines our UI

data.body:
## Today
- Visualizer identifiers are distinct from archetype names
    - but **most** of the time identical
- Visualizers are selected heuristically based on archetype indicators
- Visualizers can be set explicitly via `VisualizerOverrides`

### Points of friction

- visualizers are a separate and under-documented concept
- `VisualizerOverrides` has informal list of visualizer strings that is not kept up to date and doesn't show up anywhere else
- tagged components go away - how to decide visualizer when names are conflicting?


## Solution: correlation of archetypes & visualizers

Each visualizer can be described by a name & a list of components, i.e. they _are_ archetypes already.

-> Some archetypes don't have a visualizer - e.g. `Scalar`
-> Separate “required for logging” & “required for visualizing” - `Scalar` is required to visualize point/line, so we won't offer it automatically. But logging `SeriesLine` doesn't require `Scalar` and the presence of its tag still brings the visualizer into existence.

Going forward, some archetypes may have to be split up:
There can be a "base" archetype for mesh data and additional components in a `MeshWireframe`
Note that the base archetype is typically the "raw data" and may be standardized in sorbet much earlier, whereas the extending "visualizer archetype" may follow later.

We likely want some kind of codegen supported ‘extends’ construct to better express this, _potentially_ with specially generated code & docs.

## Setting visualizers

`VisualizerOverrides` 's possible values are any archetype name which is visualizable.

Default heuristic for enabling visualizers is governed by the presence of any matching archetype name in any tag on a given entity.
A store subscriber gathers this data → replaces “indicated component concept”

Beyond that there can still be arbitrary heuristics that for instance ensure that a `Scalar` is shown with `SeriesPoint`

## TODOs

* [x] Remove visualizer identifiers and replace them with archetype names
* [x] Adjust docs & functionality `VisualizerOverrides` accordingly
* [ ] remove `VisualizerSystem::visualizer_query_info` as it is fully governed by the matching archetype definition
     * [ ] split concept of "requried for visualizing" & "required for logging", add `Scalar` to `SeriesPoint` & `SeriesLine` accordingly
* [ ] (upon removal of indicators:) change indicated entities to look for any archetype name being set
* [ ] Ensure docs reflect all of the above

## Future work

- `Transform3D` should probably split out `TransformArrows3D` which is a different visualizer. How to make it easy to set this on an existing `Transform3D` (Short term: rename the visualizer), are the ergonomics of this fine?
- Is there a more generic concept of tag overrides? (instead of `VisualizerOverrides`)
- do we still need explicit indicator-like thing in some places to easily enable visualizers
    - conceptually: entity path + tag should just work
    - some kind of new static data?


---

Full internal meeting notes this is based on:
https://www.notion.so/rerunio/Visualizers-tagged-components-157b24554b1980e2950fdc88d9e9a7d4

data.title: Customizable descriptions of displayed data

labels.name: 🟦 blueprint
labels.description: The data that defines our UI

labels.name: user-request
labels.description: This is a pressing issue for one of our users

data.body:
Closely related to:
- https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/2701 

_**Summary:**_
It would be useful having a mechanism to add custom descriptions of the data displayed in each view. These would serve as a documentation of each view, from the perspective of a user wanting to interpret what's displayed there.

This would be different from information logged with the data itself. Each logged dataset can be displayed in different views, and the semantics of how those data are displayed changes in each view (simple example, a time series might have different colors and associated meaning in each view it's plotted in).

_**Current solution:**_
Our workaround is very simple right now: all this documentation is collected in an MD document and displayed to the users in a single text view. This gets the job done, but is disconnected from the views - it requires the user to manually find the section in the MD that corresponds to the view they want to understand.

I've considered logging a separate MD for each view and display it in the UI right next to the corresponding views, but with dozens of views we're using this would add more clutter to an already cluttered UI - especially that we heavily rely on tab groups to manage all this content.

_**Proposed solution:**_
Adding a generic editable "Description" field to each view. This could be edited manually directly in the UI, or from code in case of programmatically generated blueprints. This would be displayed when the view is selected, in the right-hand panel along with the other properties of that view.

Sketch below - the selected view in pink frame could have the description displayed as indicated by the green frame,

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06bdd287-1b63-4820-8eff-839a43f67a96)

data.body:
**Describe the bug**
I spawn 2 recordings in the same application then I log one archetype in both recording.
Then I send **different** blueprints to both recording. But it looks like both recordings receive the same blueprint.
 
In the example below, the content of the `Spacial3DView` of the first recording is `+ /point2` instead of `+ /point1`.
```py
import rerun.blueprint as rrb
import rerun as rr

rec1 = rr.new_recording("my_app", recording_id="s1", spawn=True)
rr.log(
    "point1",
    rr.Points3D(
        [[0, 1, 0]],
        radii=[0.1, 0.3],
        colors=[0, 0, 255],
    ),
    recording=rec1
)

rec2 = rr.new_recording("my_app", recording_id="s2", spawn=True)
rr.log(
    "point2",
    rr.Points3D(
        [[1, 1, 1]],
        radii=[0.1, 0.3],
        colors=[0, 0, 255],
    ),
    recording=rec2
)

rr.send_blueprint(
    rrb.Spatial3DView(contents=["+ /point1"]),
    recording=rec1,
)
rr.send_blueprint(
    rrb.Spatial3DView(contents=["+ /point2"]),
    recording=rec2,
)
```

If the two recordings are both in a different application it works correctly.

data.title: Support arbitrary X axis in the plot view using a `ScalarAbscissa`
data.body:
This [discord thread](https://discord.com/channels/1062300748202921994/1312444177304256512/1312444177304256512) got me thinking and I'd like to suggest this alternative take on:
- https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/5622

In this discussion, the user wanted to store an entire 2D plot in each frame of their simulation result, and resorted to logging a matplotlib raster:

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4b18a779-0d67-40c2-bfca-5d82f5669f5e)


**Note**: this proposal address the (possibly time-varying) "instantaneous" plot use case, aka the use case where the entire plot (X and Y axis) is stored at a single time point (modulo latest at). It does not address the case where one time varying scalar must be plotted against another time varying scalar.

### Core proposal

The core proposal is to introduce a `ScalarAbscissa` component (someone please finds a better name) that is essentially a `Scalar` component to be used as X axis (with [tagged components](#6889) we could actually reuse the same `Scalar` component).

Then, the existing Timeseries view would be altered as follows:

- Renamed to `Plot view`.
- When used in Latest At mode: plot the `Scalar` component (which, in this case, should typically be a n>1 batch) against the `ScalarAbscissa` component. 
- When used in Range mode: no modifications w.r.t to the current behaviour. (For a given time point, if the `Scalar` is a batch, pick instance at index 0 and ignore others. Also, ignore `ScalarAbscissa`.)

### `Scalar` x `ScalarAbscissa` join

- Obviously, we have basic instance join semantics.
- The resulting plot has a number of point which is the min of both components (if `Scalar`as 10 instance and `ScalarAbscissa` as 15, then we plot 10 points).
- The fallback provider for `ScalarAbscissa` is `range(n)` where `n = len(Scalar)`.
- If multiple entities are added to the plot view, each `Scalar` are matched against the collocated `ScalarAbscissa` (if any). In other words, not cross-entity shenanigans (*)

(*) this is a bit of a limitation in the case of many series against the same abscissa. Possible workaround:
- allow 2d tensors to be considered a collection of multiple scalars
- allow multiple scalars to be collocated using tagged components
- allow any vecXD-based component to be plottable

### Bonus features

- When in Range mode with n>1 `Scalar` batches, have some options to display a compound value for each point (mean/media with stddev bars, box plot, etc.)
- …

### Related

- https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/1387
- https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/1630
- https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/5622
- https://github.com/rerun-io/rerun/issues/7346
